Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verse 1:

[Page 207]
Surat al-Zumar
Seventy-five verses, Meccan

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere religion. And those who take protectors other than Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [continually] ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Exalted is He! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

And those who take protectors other than Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾

Know that in this verse there are several issues:

The first issue: al-Farra' (a early grammarian of Kufa) and al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and Qur'an scholar) mentioned two possibilities regarding the nominative case of "tanzil" (revelation):

One of them: that the phrase "tanzil" is the subject (mubtada'), and the phrase "min Allah al-'Aziz al-Hakim" (from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise) is the predicate (khabar).

The second: that the estimated sense is: "This is the revelation of the Book," so the subject is omitted, as in His saying: ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾ [al-Nur: 1], i.e., "This is a surah." Some of them preferred the first view for several reasons:

The first: omission (idmar) is contrary to the original form, so it is not resorted to except out of necessity, and there is no necessity here.

The second: when we say "The revelation of the Book is from Allah" as a complete sentence of subject and predicate, it conveys a noble benefit, namely that the revelation of the Book is from Allah and not from anyone else, and this restriction (hasr) is a meaningful notion. If we omit the subject, this benefit is not achieved.

[Page 208]
The third: if we omit the subject, the sense becomes: "This is the revelation of the Book from Allah," and then we are obliged to another metaphor, because "this" refers to the surah, and the surah is not the very revelation; rather the surah is revealed. Then we must say that the verbal noun is meant as the object (maf'ul), which is a metaphor we have assumed without necessity.

The second issue: Those who hold that the Qur'an is created argued by saying: Indeed, He, the Exalted, described the Qur'an as being "revelation" (tanzil) and "revealed" (munazzal), and this attribute befits only what is created and originated. The answer: We interpret this word as referring to the letters and the expressions (al-siyagh wa al-huruf).

The third issue: Many verses indicate that the Qur'an is described as "tanzil," and other verses indicate that it is "munazzal."

As for the first: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192]; and He said: ﴿A revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]; and He said: ﴿Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 2].

As for the second: His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder﴾ [al-Hijr: 9], and He said: ﴿And with truth We have sent it down, and with truth it descended﴾ [al-Isra': 105]. You know that its being "munazzal" (sent down) is closer to the reality than its being "tanzil," so its being "munazzal" is also a metaphor, because if by the Qur'an is meant the attribute subsisting in the Essence of Allah, then it does not admit separation or descent; and if by it is meant the letters and sounds, then they are accidents that do not admit movement or descent. Rather, by the descent is meant the descent of the angel who conveyed them to the Messenger ﷺ.

The fourth issue: The Mu'tazilah said: "al-'Aziz" is the Capable who cannot be overcome, so this word indicates that He, the Exalted, is capable of what has no limit. And "al-Hakim" is the one who acts due to the motive of wisdom, not due to the motive of desire. This is only complete if it is established that He, the Exalted, has knowledge of all knowable things and that He is free from need of all needs. Once this is established, we say: His being "'Aziz and Hakim" indicates these three attributes: knowledge of all knowable things, power over all possible things, and independence from all needs. Whoever is like this cannot do what is ugly nor judge by what is ugly, and whatever he does is wisdom and rightness. Once this is established, we say: benefiting from the Qur'an depends on two principles:

One of them: that it is known that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah. The evidence for it is that the Messenger's truthfulness was established by the miracle, and it was established by mass transmission (tawatur) that he used to say: "The Qur'an is the speech of Allah." From the combination of these two premises it follows that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah.

The second principle: that Allah intended by these words the meanings they are set for, either according to the language, or according to the customary or legal indication, because if He did not intend those, it would be deception, and that is not fitting for the Wise. From what we have mentioned, it is established that benefiting from the Qur'an is not achieved except after accepting these two principles, and it is established that there is no way to prove these two principles except by proving that He, the Exalted, is Wise, and it is established that there is no way to prove His being Wise except by building on His being 'Aziz, the Exalted. For this reason He said: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, there are two questions in it:

The first question: The word "tanzil" implies that He, the Exalted, sent it down to him gradually, part by part, while the word "inzal" implies that He sent it down to him in one single go. So how are both reconciled? The answer: If the distinction between "tanzil" and "inzal" is valid in the way you mentioned, then the way to reconcile them is to say: the meaning is that We decided with a comprehensive and definite decision that this Book should reach you, and this is the "inzal"; then We delivered it to you part by part in accordance with the interests, and this is the "tanzil."

[Page 209]
The second question: What is meant by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾? The answer: There are two views:

The first: It means that We sent down the Book to you accompanied by truth, rectitude and correctness, in the sense that everything We placed in it of establishing the Oneness of God, prophethood, the Return, and kinds of obligations is true and right, which must be acted upon and adhered to.

The second: that what is meant is "Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book" on the basis of a true proof which shows that the Book descends from Allah, and that proof is that the eloquent people were unable to produce its equal, and if it were not a miracle they would not have been unable to oppose it.

Then He said: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾. And in this there are several issues:

The first issue: When He, exalted is He, had explained in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾ that this Book comprises truth, sincerity and correctness, He followed up with some of what it contains of truth and sincerity, which is that a person should occupy himself with worshipping Allah, exalted is He, in the manner of sincerity, and should completely disassociate himself from worshipping other than Allah, exalted is He. His occupying himself with worshipping Allah, exalted is He, in the manner of sincerity is what is meant by His saying: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere﴾; and his disassociation from worshipping other than Allah, exalted is He, is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere religion﴾, because His saying ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah﴾ conveys restriction (ḥaṣr). The meaning of restriction is that the judgment is established for what is mentioned and negated from what is not mentioned. Know that worship together with sincerity cannot be truly understood unless we know what worship is, what sincerity is, and what the factors contrary to sincerity are. These are three matters which must be investigated:

As for worship ('ibādah): it is an act, or a statement, or the abandonment of an act, or the abandonment of a statement, and it is performed merely from the belief that the command to it is great and that its acceptance is obligatory.

As for sincerity (ikhlāṣ): it is that the motive for performing that act or abandonment is merely this submission and obedience. If another motive arises in him, then either the side of the motive toward obedience is stronger than the other side, or equal to it, or weaker. They agreed that the equal and the weaker side is void. As for when the motive toward obedience to Allah is stronger than the other side, they differed over whether it is valid or not, and we have mentioned this issue repeatedly. The wording of the Qur'an indicates the obligation of performing it in the manner of purity, because His saying ﴿So worship Allah, sincere﴾ is explicit that worship must be performed in the manner of purity. This is reinforced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5].

As for explaining the factors contrary to sincerity: they are the motives that call toward a partner, and they are of several kinds:
First: that showing off (riyā') and seeking reputation (sum'ah) have a role in it.
Second: that his aim in performing the act of obedience is attaining Paradise and deliverance from the Fire.
Third: that he performs it and believes that it has an effect in bringing about reward or averting punishment.
Fourth: that he purifies the acts of obedience from major sins so that they become accepted; and this statement is only considered according to the view of the Mu'tazilah.

The second issue: Some people have said: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ means the testimony that there is no god but Allah. They argued with what is related: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no god but Allah" is my fortress, and whoever enters my fortress is safe from My punishment. This is the view of those who say that sin does not harm along with faith, just as obedience does not benefit along with disbelief. But most scholars said: the verse encompasses everything Allah has obligated through commands and prohibitions, and this is more appropriate, because His saying ﴿So worship Allah﴾ is general. It is related that when the wife of al-Farazdaq was near death, she directed that al-Hasan al-Basri pray over her. When he had prayed over her and she was buried, he said to al-Farazdaq: "O Abu Firas, what have you prepared for this matter?" He said: "The testimony that there is no god but Allah." Al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "This is the pole, so where is the rope?"

صفحة ٢١٠

This shows that the pole of a tent is not benefited from except with the tent-ropes, so that the tent can be used. The Qadi said: As for what is related, that he ﷺ said to Mu'adh and Abu al-Darda': "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals, in spite of the nose of Abu al-Darda'," if it is authentic, then it must be interpreted with the condition of repentance; otherwise this report is not accepted, because it contradicts the Qur'an, and because it requires that a person not be restrained from adultery and theft, and that he not be transgressing by committing them, since with his intense desire for the ugly he knows that it will not harm him while he adheres to the two testimonies, so that would be an incitement to the ugly. We say: whoever believes that his harm is removed by repentance has believed that committing the ugly is harmful, except that he removes that harm by performing repentance, unlike the view of one who says that committing the ugly does not harm while adhering to the two testimonies. This is the end of the Qadi's speech. It is said to him: As for your statement that the view of forgiveness contradicts the Qur'an, it is not so; rather the Qur'an indicates it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48], and He said: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6], meaning: in the state of their wrongdoing, as one says: "I saw the Amir at his eating and drinking," meaning: while he was eating and drinking. And He said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. As for your statement that this necessitates incitement to the ugly, it is said to him: If the matter were so, then His forgiving would be rationally ugly, and this is the doctrine of the Baghdadi Mu'tazilah, which you do not hold, because the doctrine of the Basrans is that the punishment of the sinner is rationally permissible. Furthermore, it would necessarily follow that forgiveness would not be attained by repentance, because if one knows that if he sins and then repents Allah will forgive him, he will not desist. As for the distinction the Qadi mentioned, it is far-fetched, because if he resolves to repent of it immediately, he knows that that sin will absolutely not harm him.

Then we say: Our doctrine is that we are certain of the occurrence of pardon for major sins in general, but as for each individual person, that is uncertain, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. So He affirmed with certainty the occurrence of forgiveness in general, but He, glorified is He and exalted, did not affirm with certainty the occurrence of this forgiveness for everyone, but for whomever He wills. Since that is so, fear remains present, and therefore incitement does not occur. And Allah knows best.

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: "al-Din" has been read in the nominative (al-dīnu). Then he said: The one who reads it in the nominative should properly read "mukhlaṣan" with a fatḥah on the lām, in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they made their religion sincere to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 146], so that it corresponds to His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere religion﴾. "Al-khāliṣ" and "al-mukhlaṣ" are one and the same, except that he described the religion with the attribute of its owner by way of metaphorical attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī), like their saying: "the poetry of a poet."

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the head and chief of acts of worship is sincerity in monotheism, He followed it with censure of the method of the polytheists, saying: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him, [saying]: "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position"﴾. The construction of the sentence is: "And those who take protectors besides Him, saying: 'We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.'" On this construction, the predicate of "alladhīna" is omitted, namely His saying "yaqūlūna" (saying). Know that the pronoun in His saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ refers to the things that were worshipped besides Allah, and these are of two kinds: rational beings and non-rational beings. As for the rational beings, some people worshipped the Messiah, 'Uzayr and the angels, and many people worship the sun, the moon and the stars, believing that they are living, rational, speaking beings. As for the things that were worshipped while not being described as living and rational, these are the idols. Having known this, we say: the statement the disbelievers mentioned is fitting for rational beings, but not fitting for non-rational beings, and its explanation is from two aspects:

The first: the pronoun in His saying: ﴿We worship them﴾ is a pronoun for rational beings, so it is not fitting for idols.

The second: it is not improbable that those disbelievers believed that they would bring them nearer to Allah, and on this supposition their intention is that their worship of them brings them nearer to Allah. It may be said that the rational person does not worship the idol insofar as it is wood or stone, but they worship it because they believe that it are images of the stars, or images of the celestial spirits, or images of the prophets and righteous ones who have passed away, and their intention in worshipping them is to direct those acts of worship to those things of which they made these images the forms.

The summary of the argument of the idol-worshippers is that they said: the Supreme God is too exalted for humans to worship Him, but it is fitting for humans to occupy themselves with worshipping the great servants of Allah, such as the stars and the celestial spirits, and then they occupy themselves with worshipping the Greatest God. This is what is meant by their saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾.

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, related their doctrines, He answered them in several ways:

The first: He limited Himself in the answer to mere threat, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ﴾. Know that when a person in error mentions a false doctrine and is persistent in it, the method of treating him is to employ a stratagem that brings about the removal of that persistence from his heart. Once persistence has been removed from his heart, afterward one makes him hear the proof that demonstrates its falsity, and this method leads more effectively to the goal. The physicians say: the ripening remedy must be administered before the purgative, for by taking the ripening agent the corrupt humours become soft and capable of removal, and when you then give him the purgative, complete cleansing is achieved. Likewise here, hearing the threat and intimidation first is like administering the ripening agent first, and hearing the proof second is like administering the purgative second. This is the benefit of placing this threat first.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar, a disbeliever﴾. The meaning is that whoever persists in lying and disbelief remains deprived of guidance. And by this lie is meant their description of these idols as deities deserving worship, while knowing that they are base inanimate objects, which they themselves carved and manipulated; and the necessary knowledge is established that describing these things with divinity is pure falsehood. As for disbelief, it may be that what is meant is disbelief that pertains to belief, and the matter here is also so, for their description of them with divinity is a lie, and their belief in their divinity is ignorance and disbelief.

It may also be that what is meant is ingratitude for favor (kufr al-ni'mah), and the reason for this is that worship is the utmost of glorification, and the utmost glorification is fitting only for one from whom the utmost bounty proceeds, and that Benefactor is Allah, glorified is He, while these idols have no part in that bounty; so occupying oneself with worshipping these idols necessitates ingratitude toward the true Benefactor.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The purpose of this statement is to establish compelling proofs that He is exalted above having a son, and its explanation is from several aspects:

The first: that had He taken a son, He would have been content only with the most perfect of children, which is a male, so how do you attribute daughters to Him?

The second: that He, glorified is He, is a true unity, and a true unity cannot have a son. As for His being a true unity: if He were composite, He would have needed each of His parts, and His part is other than Him, so He would have needed other than Himself, and that which needs other than itself is possible in its essence, and that which is possible in its essence cannot be necessary of existence in its essence. As for the one not having a son, it is for several reasons:

The first: a son is a part of the parts of a thing that separates from it, and then there comes to be for it a form equal to the form of the parent; and this is conceivable only in a thing from which a part separates, while the absolute single entity is not described by that.

The second: the condition for a child is that it be similar to the parent in the complete quiddity (ma'hiyyah), so that the reality of that thing would be a specific nature (haqiqah nw'iyyah) predicated of two individuals. And that is impossible. For if the specification of each of the two is among the necessary attributes of that quiddity, it would follow that only one individual could come into existence from that quiddity; and if that specification is not among the necessary attributes of that quiddity, then that specification would be known through a separate cause, and so He would not be a God who necessarily exists by His own essence. Thus it is established that His being a God who necessarily exists by His essence requires His being one in His reality, and His being one in His reality prevents a child from being ascribed to Him. Thus it is established that His being one prevents the existence of a child.

The third: a child comes into being only from a husband and a wife, and the spouses must be of one kind. So if He had a child, He would not be one; rather, His wife would be of His kind. As for His being Irresistible (qahhar) preventing a child from being ascribed to Him, that is because the one in need of a child is the one who dies, so he needs a child to take his place. The one in need of a child is the one who is subdued by death. As for the one who is Irresistible and is not subdued by anything else, a child is impossible in his case. Thus it is established that His words ﴿He is Allah, the One, the Irresistible﴾ are expressions containing decisive proofs negating a child from Allah, exalted is He.

Having known this, we say: the statement the disbelievers mentioned is fitting for rational beings, but not fitting for non-rational beings, and its explanation is from two aspects:

The first: the pronoun in His saying: ﴿We worship them﴾ is a pronoun for rational beings, so it is not fitting for idols.

The second: it is not improbable that those disbelievers believed that they would bring them nearer to Allah, and on this supposition their intention is that their worship of them brings them nearer to Allah. It may be said that the rational person does not worship the idol insofar as it is wood or stone, but they worship it because they believe that it are images of the stars, or images of the celestial spirits, or images of the prophets and righteous ones who have passed away, and their intention in worshipping them is to direct those acts of worship to those things of which they made these images the forms.

The summary of the argument of the idol-worshippers is that they said: the Supreme God is too exalted for humans to worship Him, but it is fitting for humans to occupy themselves with worshipping the great servants of Allah, such as the stars and the celestial spirits, and then they occupy themselves with worshipping the Greatest God. This is what is meant by their saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾.

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, related their doctrines, He answered them in several ways:

The first: He limited Himself in the answer to mere threat, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ﴾. Know that when a person in error mentions a false doctrine and is persistent in it, the method of treating him is to employ a stratagem that brings about the removal of that persistence from his heart. Once persistence has been removed from his heart, afterward one makes him hear the proof that demonstrates its falsity, and this method leads more effectively to the goal. The physicians say: the ripening remedy must be administered before the purgative, for by taking the ripening agent the corrupt humours become soft and capable of removal, and when you then give him the purgative, complete cleansing is achieved. Likewise here, hearing the threat and intimidation first is like administering the ripening agent first, and hearing the proof second is like administering the purgative second. This is the benefit of placing this threat first.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar, a disbeliever﴾. The meaning is that whoever persists in lying and disbelief remains deprived of guidance. And by this lie is meant their description of these idols as deities deserving worship, while knowing that they are base inanimate objects, which they themselves carved and manipulated; and the necessary knowledge is established that describing these things with divinity is pure falsehood. As for disbelief, it may be that what is meant is disbelief that pertains to belief, and the matter here is also so, for their description of them with divinity is a lie, and their belief in their divinity is ignorance and disbelief.

It may also be that what is meant is ingratitude for favor (kufr al-ni'mah), and the reason for this is that worship is the utmost of glorification, and the utmost glorification is fitting only for one from whom the utmost bounty proceeds, and that Benefactor is Allah, glorified is He, while these idols have no part in that bounty; so occupying oneself with worshipping these idols necessitates ingratitude toward the true Benefactor.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen whom He willed from what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. The purpose of this statement is to establish compelling proofs that He is exalted above having a son, and its explanation is from several aspects:

The first: that had He taken a son, He would have been content only with the most perfect of children, which is a male, so how do you attribute daughters to Him?

The second: that He, glorified is He, is a true unity, and a true unity cannot have a son. As for His being a true unity: if He were composite, He would have needed each of His parts, and His part is other than Him, so He would have needed other than Himself, and that which needs other than itself is possible in its essence, and that which is possible in its essence cannot be necessary of existence in its essence. As for the one not having a son, it is for several reasons:

The first: a son is a part of the parts of a thing that separates from it, and then there comes to be for it a form equal to the form of the parent; and this is conceivable only in a thing from which a part separates, while the absolute single entity is not described by that.

The second: the condition for a child is that it be similar to the parent in the complete quiddity (ma'hiyyah), so that the reality of that thing would be a specific nature (haqiqah nw'iyyah) predicated of two individuals. And that is impossible. For if the specification of each of the two is among the necessary attributes of that quiddity, it would follow that only one individual could come into existence from that quiddity; and if that specification is not among the necessary attributes of that quiddity, then that specification would be known through a separate cause, and so He would not be a God who necessarily exists by His own essence. Thus it is established that His being a God who necessarily exists by His essence requires His being one in His reality, and His being one in His reality prevents a child from being ascribed to Him. Thus it is established that His being one prevents the existence of a child.

The third: a child comes into being only from a husband and a wife, and the spouses must be of one kind. So if He had a child, He would not be one; rather, His wife would be of His kind. As for His being Irresistible (qahhar) preventing a child from being ascribed to Him, that is because the one in need of a child is the one who dies, so he needs a child to take his place. The one in need of a child is the one who is subdued by death. As for the one who is Irresistible and is not subdued by anything else, a child is impossible in his case. Thus it is established that His words ﴿He is Allah, the One, the Irresistible﴾ are expressions containing decisive proofs negating a child from Allah, exalted is He.

Then He said: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾. And in this there are several issues:

The first issue: When He, exalted is He, had explained in His saying ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾ that this Book comprises truth, sincerity and correctness, He followed up with some of what it contains of truth and sincerity, which is that a person should occupy himself with worshipping Allah, exalted is He, in the manner of sincerity, and should completely disassociate himself from worshipping other than Allah, exalted is He. His occupying himself with worshipping Allah, exalted is He, in the manner of sincerity is what is meant by His saying: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere﴾; and his disassociation from worshipping other than Allah, exalted is He, is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere religion﴾, because His saying ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah﴾ conveys restriction (ḥaṣr). The meaning of restriction is that the judgment is established for what is mentioned and negated from what is not mentioned. Know that worship together with sincerity cannot be truly understood unless we know what worship is, what sincerity is, and what the factors contrary to sincerity are. These are three matters which must be investigated:

As for worship ('ibādah): it is an act, or a statement, or the abandonment of an act, or the abandonment of a statement, and it is performed merely from the belief that the command to it is great and that its acceptance is obligatory.

As for sincerity (ikhlāṣ): it is that the motive for performing that act or abandonment is merely this submission and obedience. If another motive arises in him, then either the side of the motive toward obedience is stronger than the other side, or equal to it, or weaker. They agreed that the equal and the weaker side is void. As for when the motive toward obedience to Allah is stronger than the other side, they differed over whether it is valid or not, and we have mentioned this issue repeatedly. The wording of the Qur'an indicates the obligation of performing it in the manner of purity, because His saying ﴿So worship Allah, sincere﴾ is explicit that worship must be performed in the manner of purity. This is reinforced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5].

As for explaining the factors contrary to sincerity: they are the motives that call toward a partner, and they are of several kinds:
First: that showing off (riyā') and seeking reputation (sum'ah) have a role in it.
Second: that his aim in performing the act of obedience is attaining Paradise and deliverance from the Fire.
Third: that he performs it and believes that it has an effect in bringing about reward or averting punishment.
Fourth: that he purifies the acts of obedience from major sins so that they become accepted; and this statement is only considered according to the view of the Mu'tazilah.

The second issue: Some people have said: ﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ means the testimony that there is no god but Allah. They argued with what is related: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no god but Allah" is my fortress, and whoever enters my fortress is safe from My punishment. This is the view of those who say that sin does not harm along with faith, just as obedience does not benefit along with disbelief. But most scholars said: the verse encompasses everything Allah has obligated through commands and prohibitions, and this is more appropriate, because His saying ﴿So worship Allah﴾ is general. It is related that when the wife of al-Farazdaq was near death, she directed that al-Hasan al-Basri pray over her. When he had prayed over her and she was buried, he said to al-Farazdaq: "O Abu Firas, what have you prepared for this matter?" He said: "The testimony that there is no god but Allah." Al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "This is the pole, so where is the rope?"

صفحة ٢١٠

This shows that the pole of a tent is not benefited from except with the tent-ropes, so that the tent can be used. The Qadi said: As for what is related, that he ﷺ said to Mu'adh and Abu al-Darda': "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals, in spite of the nose of Abu al-Darda'," if it is authentic, then it must be interpreted with the condition of repentance; otherwise this report is not accepted, because it contradicts the Qur'an, and because it requires that a person not be restrained from adultery and theft, and that he not be transgressing by committing them, since with his intense desire for the ugly he knows that it will not harm him while he adheres to the two testimonies, so that would be an incitement to the ugly. We say: whoever believes that his harm is removed by repentance has believed that committing the ugly is harmful, except that he removes that harm by performing repentance, unlike the view of one who says that committing the ugly does not harm while adhering to the two testimonies. This is the end of the Qadi's speech. It is said to him: As for your statement that the view of forgiveness contradicts the Qur'an, it is not so; rather the Qur'an indicates it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48], and He said: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6], meaning: in the state of their wrongdoing, as one says: "I saw the Amir at his eating and drinking," meaning: while he was eating and drinking. And He said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. As for your statement that this necessitates incitement to the ugly, it is said to him: If the matter were so, then His forgiving would be rationally ugly, and this is the doctrine of the Baghdadi Mu'tazilah, which you do not hold, because the doctrine of the Basrans is that the punishment of the sinner is rationally permissible. Furthermore, it would necessarily follow that forgiveness would not be attained by repentance, because if one knows that if he sins and then repents Allah will forgive him, he will not desist. As for the distinction the Qadi mentioned, it is far-fetched, because if he resolves to repent of it immediately, he knows that that sin will absolutely not harm him.

Then we say: Our doctrine is that we are certain of the occurrence of pardon for major sins in general, but as for each individual person, that is uncertain, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. So He affirmed with certainty the occurrence of forgiveness in general, but He, glorified is He and exalted, did not affirm with certainty the occurrence of this forgiveness for everyone, but for whomever He wills. Since that is so, fear remains present, and therefore incitement does not occur. And Allah knows best.

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: "al-Din" has been read in the nominative (al-dīnu). Then he said: The one who reads it in the nominative should properly read "mukhlaṣan" with a fatḥah on the lām, in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they made their religion sincere to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 146], so that it corresponds to His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere religion﴾. "Al-khāliṣ" and "al-mukhlaṣ" are one and the same, except that he described the religion with the attribute of its owner by way of metaphorical attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī), like their saying: "the poetry of a poet."

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the head and chief of acts of worship is sincerity in monotheism, He followed it with censure of the method of the polytheists, saying: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him, [saying]: "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position"﴾. The construction of the sentence is: "And those who take protectors besides Him, saying: 'We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.'" On this construction, the predicate of "alladhīna" is omitted, namely His saying "yaqūlūna" (saying). Know that the pronoun in His saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ refers to the things that were worshipped besides Allah, and these are of two kinds: rational beings and non-rational beings. As for the rational beings, some people worshipped the Messiah, 'Uzayr and the angels, and many people worship the sun, the moon and the stars, believing that they are living, rational, speaking beings. As for the things that were worshipped while not being described as living and rational, these are the idols. This is the benefit of placing this threat first.

He said, may He be exalted: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Ever-Forgiving.﴾ ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you, and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. But if you are thankful, He approves it for you. No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knower of what is in the breasts.﴾

Know that the preceding verse indicated that He, exalted, demonstrated His being free of offspring through His being one God and a Subduer, dominant, that is, of perfect power. When He established that matter upon these principles, He mentioned after it what indicates perfect power and perfect self-sufficiency. Also, He, exalted, criticized the divinity of idols, so He mentioned after it the attributes by which divinity is realized. Know that we have explained in several places of this book that the proofs which God, exalted, mentioned to establish His divinity are either celestial (falakiyyah) or elemental (unsuriyyah). As for the celestial proofs, they are of several kinds:

The first: the creation of the heavens and the earth. This meaning indicates the existence of the Powerful God from many aspects, which we explained in the commentary on His saying, exalted: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

[p. 213]

The second: the alternation of the states of night and day, and this is what is meant here by His saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾. This is because light and darkness are two awesome, great armies, and each day one of them overcomes the other at times, and the other overcomes it at other times. This indicates that each of them is overcome and subdued, and there must be a dominant Subduer over both, under whose management and dominion they are, and He is God, glorified and exalted. The meaning of this "wrapping" is that He adds to each of them by the amount that the other loses. As for the meaning of the wrapping of night and day, it is what was narrated in the hadith: "We seek refuge in God from al-hawr after al-kawr," meaning from turning back after advancing. Know that He, glorified and exalted, expressed this meaning by His saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day﴾, and by His saying: ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and by His saying: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ [al-Hajj: 61], and by His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember﴾ [al-Furqan: 62].

The third: considering the states of the stars, especially the sun and the moon, for the sun is the sultan of the day and the moon is the sultan of the night, and most of the interests of this world are bound to them. His saying: ﴿each runs for a specified term﴾: the specified term is the Day of Resurrection. They continue to run until this day, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be gone. Its parallel is His saying, exalted: ﴿and the sun and the moon are joined﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 9]. The meaning of this subjection is that these spheres revolve like the revolving of a waterwheel (manjanun) in one fixed manner until the Day of Resurrection, and at that time the sky will be folded up like the folding of a scroll for documents.

When God mentioned these three types of celestial proofs, He said: ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Ever-Forgiving.﴾ The meaning is that the creation of these great bodies, although it indicates that He is Mighty, that is, of perfect power, He is also Ever-Forgiving, of great mercy, bounty, and beneficence. For when information about His being of great power produces fear and awe, His being Ever-Forgiving produces abundant mercy, and abundant mercy produces hope and desire. Then He, exalted, followed the mention of the celestial proofs with the mention of proofs drawn from this lower world. He began with mentioning the human being, saying: ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾. The proof of the human being's coming into existence as indicating the God who chooses has been explained many times before.

If it is said: How is it permissible to say ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾ when the mate was created before their creation? They answered this from several aspects:

The first: just as the word "then" (thumma) comes to indicate that one of two events occurred later than the second, so too it comes to indicate that one of two statements is later than the other, like the speaker's saying: "What you did today has reached me, then what you did yesterday was more astonishing," and he also says: "I gave you something today, then what I gave you yesterday was more."

The second: that the sense is "He created you from a soul that was created alone, then its mate was made from it."

The third: God, exalted, brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back like particles (dharr), then after that He created Eve.

Know that when He, exalted, mentioned the argument from His creation of the human being for the existence of the Creator, He mentioned after it the argument from the existence of animals for Him, saying: ﴿and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾. These are: camels, cattle, sheep, and goats. We have explained how these animals indicate the existence of the Creator in His saying: ﴿and the livestock, He created them for you; in them is warmth﴾ [al-Nahl: 5]. Regarding His saying: ﴿and He sent down for you﴾, there are several aspects:

The first: that God's decree, His determination, and His judgment are described as descending from heaven, because He wrote in the Preserved Tablet every existent that will exist.

The second: that none of the animals lives except by plants, and plants do not subsist except by water and soil, and water descends from heaven. So the sense becomes as if He sent them down.

The third: that He, exalted, created them in Paradise and then sent them down to the earth. His saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾ means a male and a female of the camel, cattle, sheep, and goats. The word "pair" (zawj) is a name for each one that has another with it; when it stands alone, it is a single (fard) of that. He, exalted, said: ﴿and He made from it the two mates, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 39].

[p. 214]

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, and in this there are discussions:

The first: Hamzah read "ummahatikum" with a kasrah on the alif and the mim; al-Kisa'i read it with a kasrah on the hamzah and a fatḥah on the mim; and the rest read "ummahatikum" with a ḍammah on the alif and a fatḥah on the mim.

The second: when He, exalted, mentioned the creation of people from one person, namely Adam, peace be upon him, He followed it with the creation of livestock. He specifically mentioned them because they are the most noble of animals after the human being. Then, after mentioning these two, He mentioned a state shared between the human being and the livestock, namely their being created in the wombs of their mothers. His saying: ﴿creation after creation﴾ means what God mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We created the human being from an extract of clay﴾ ﴿then We made him a drop in a firm lodging﴾ ﴿then We created the drop a clinging clot, then We created the clot a lump, then We created the lump bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–14]. As for His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾, it has been said: the three darknesses are the belly, the womb, and the placenta. It has also been said: the loin, the womb, and the belly. The aspect of argument from these states has been explained in our commentary on His saying: ﴿He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran: 6].

Know that when He, exalted, explained these proofs and described them, He said: ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾. That is, that thing whose wondrous acts you have come to know is God, your Lord. In this verse there is an indication that He, glorified and exalted, is free of parts and limbs, and that He is free of corporeality (jismiyyah) and of being in a place (makaniyyah). This is because when He, exalted, wanted to make His servants know His particular essence, He mentioned only His being the doer of these things. Had He been a body composed of limbs, His definition by those parts and limbs would have been a definition of a thing by the parts of its reality. As for defining Him by His states, acts, and effects, that is a definition of Him by matters external to His essence, and the first definition is more complete than the second. Had that first kind been possible, relying on this second kind would have been a shortcoming and a deficiency, and that is impermissible. So we know that relying on this second kind was only good because the first kind is impossible and impossible to exist. This indicates that He, glorified and exalted, is exalted above corporeality, limbs, and parts.

* * *

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion﴾. This indicates restriction: that is, dominion belongs to Him and not to anyone else. Since it is established that there is no dominion except His, it is necessary to say that there is no god but Him, for if another god were established, that god would either have dominion or not have dominion. If he has dominion, then each of them would be an owner and a capable one, and mutual obstruction would take place between them, as established in His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than God, both would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22], and that is impossible. If the second has no part of power or dominion, then he would be deficient and not fit for divinity. So it is established that when the proof indicates that there is no dominion except for God, it is necessary to say: there is no god for the worlds and no object of worship for all creation except God, the One, the Real, the Eternal Refuge.

Then know that when He, glorified, explained with these proofs the perfection of God's power, wisdom, and mercy, He arranged upon it the refutation of the way of the polytheists and the misguided from several aspects:

The first: His saying: ﴿so how are you turned away?﴾. Our companions (the Ash'arites) argue with it, and the Mu'tazilah also argue with it. As for our companions, the aspect of argument for them from this verse is that it is explicit that they did not turn themselves away from these clear proofs; rather, someone else turned them away from them, and that other is none but God. Also, the proof of reason strengthens this, because every person wants for himself the attainment of truth and correctness. When that is not achieved, and only ignorance and misguidance occur, we know that it comes from another, not from himself. As for the Mu'tazilah, the aspect of argument for them is that His saying ﴿so how are you turned away?﴾ is an expression of wonder at this turning away, and if the agent of that turning were God, exalted, this wonder would have no meaning.

[p. 215]

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you﴾. The meaning is that God, exalted, did not impose obligations on those who are obligated in order to draw any benefit to Himself or to repel any harm from Himself, because He, exalted, is absolutely self-sufficient, and bringing benefit or repelling harm is impossible with respect to Him. We only said that He is self-sufficient for several reasons:

The first: that He is necessarily existent in His essence, and necessarily existent in all His attributes, and whoever is like this is absolutely self-sufficient.

The second: that if He were in need, that need would either be eternal or temporal. The first is false, for otherwise it would follow that He would create in eternity what He needed, and that is impossible, because creation and eternity are contradictory. The second is also false, because need is a deficiency, and the Wise One is not driven by a motive to acquire a deficiency for Himself.

The third: suppose that doubt remains as to whether craving, aversion, and need can be attributed to Him or not. Is it not known by necessity that the God who is able to create the heavens and the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the Throne, the Footstool, the four elements, and the three generated kinds (mawalid) is impossible to benefit from the prayer of Zayd and the fasting of 'Amr, and impossible to be harmed by the non-prayer of this one and the non-fasting of that one? Thus it is established by what we have mentioned that if all the worlds disbelieved and persisted in ignorance, God would still be free of need of them.

Then He, exalted, said after this: ﴿and He does not approve disbelief for His servants﴾. That is to say: although He is not benefited by belief nor harmed by disbelief, He does not approve of disbelief. Al-Jubba'i argued with this verse in two ways:

The first: the Mujbirah (determinists) say that God, exalted, created the disbelief of the servants, and that from the standpoint of what He created it is true and correct. He (al-Jubba'i) said: if the matter were so, then He would have approved disbelief from the aspect in which He created it, and that is the opposite of the verse.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verses 5–7 (part 2 of 2):

The second argument: If disbelief were by the decree of Allah the Exalted, then we would be obligated to be content with it, because contentment with the decree of Allah the Exalted is obligatory. Since the community has agreed that being content with disbelief is disbelief, it is established that it is not by the decree of Allah, and it is also not by the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. Our companions (al-Ashab, the scholars of our theological school) answered this argument in several ways:

The first: The practice of the Qur'an is to restrict the word *'ibad* (servants) to the believers. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], and He says: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan: 6], and He says: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. Accordingly, on this reading, His statement ﴿and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ means that He does not approve disbelief for the believers, and that does not harm us.

The second: We say that disbelief is by the will of Allah the Exalted, but we do not say that it is by the pleasure of Allah. This is because *ridá* (contentment, pleasure) is an expression of praise for an act and approval of it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah was certainly pleased with the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 18], meaning that He praises them and commends them.

The third: Our father, the Shaykh Diya' al-Din Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: *ridá* is an expression for abandoning blame and objection, and it is not an expression for will. The evidence for this is the verse of Ibn Durayd:

*I was content by compulsion, and contentment under compulsion is the contentment of one who was angry at the turning of fate.*

He affirmed *ridá* together with compulsion (*qasr*), and this indicates what we have said.

The fourth: Grant that *ridá* means will. Still, His statement ﴿and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ is general, so restricting it to the verses which indicate that He wills disbelief from the disbeliever is like His statement: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan: 30]. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾. The meaning is that, when He had explained that He does not approve disbelief, He explained that He approves gratitude. There are several issues here:

The first issue: The reciters differed over the *ha'* in *yarḍahu* (يَرْضَهُ) in three ways:

The first: Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Hamzah read it with a *ḍammah* on the *ha'*, *mukhtalasah* (brief, weakly pronounced) and not followed by a *waw*.

The second: Abu 'Amr and Hamzah, in some transmissions, read *yarḍah* (يَرْضَهْ) with a *sukun* on the *ha'*, for lightness.

The third: Nafi', in some transmissions, Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and al-Kisa'i read it with a *ḍammah* on the *ha'* and *mushba'ah* (fully pronounced).

Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among the reciters are those who fully pronounced the *ha'* until they attached a *waw* to it, because the letter before the *ha'* is vowelled, so it became in the position of *ḍaraba-hu* (ضَرَبَهُ) and *lahu* (لَهُ). Just as this is fully pronounced according to all, so likewise *yarḍahu* (يَرْضَهُ). Among them are those who vowelled the *ha'* and did not add the *waw*, because the original form is *yarḍāhu* (يَرْضاهُ), and the *alif* which is deleted for the *jazm* (apocopation) is not necessarily deleted, so it is like the remaining one. And with the *alif* remaining, it is not permissible to add the *waw*; so likewise here.

The second issue: Gratitude (*shukr*) is a compound state made of speech, belief and action. As for speech, it is the acknowledgment that the blessing has occurred. As for belief, it is the belief that the blessing has come from that benefactor.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾. Al-Jubba'i said: This indicates that Allah the Exalted does not punish anyone for the act of another. So if Allah created their disbelief, it would not be permissible for Him to punish them for it. Also, it is not permissible for children to be punished for the sins of their fathers, unlike what the others say. Those who deny that the blood money (*diyah*) must be imposed on the 'aqilah (paternal kin) also argued from this verse.

* * *

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾. Know that we have mentioned many times that the most important matters for a human being are: to know his Creator to the extent possible; to know what harms him and what benefits him in this worldly life; and to know his state after death. In this verse, He mentioned many proofs from the higher world and the lower world concerning the perfection of the Creator's power, knowledge and wisdom. Then He followed this by commanding gratitude and forbidding disbelief. Then He explained the state of the human after death by His saying: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾. There are issues here:

The first issue: The Mushabbihah (anthropomorphists) held onto the word *ilá* (إلى, "to") as evidence that the God of the universe is in a direction. We have answered this many times.

The second issue: The people (the proponents of the pre-existence of souls) claimed that these souls existed before the bodies, and they held onto the word "return" (*rujū'*) which occurs in this verse and in other verses.

The third issue: This verse indicates the affirmation of resurrection (*ba'th*) and the Last Day (*qiyamah*).

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾. This is a warning to the disobedient and good news to the obedient. His statement, ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, serves as the reason for what preceded it. That is, He is able to inform you of your deeds, because He is knowing of all that is known. So He knows what is in your hearts of motives and deterrents. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not look at your forms or your words, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds."

[Page 216]

He said, may He be exalted: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Ever-Forgiving.﴾ ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed God is free of need of you, and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. But if you are thankful, He approves it for you. No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knower of what is in the breasts.﴾

Know that the preceding verse indicated that He, exalted, demonstrated His being free of offspring through His being one God and a Subduer, dominant, that is, of perfect power. When He established that matter upon these principles, He mentioned after it what indicates perfect power and perfect self-sufficiency. Also, He, exalted, criticized the divinity of idols, so He mentioned after it the attributes by which divinity is realized. Know that we have explained in several places of this book that the proofs which God, exalted, mentioned to establish His divinity are either celestial (falakiyyah) or elemental (unsuriyyah). As for the celestial proofs, they are of several kinds:

The first: the creation of the heavens and the earth. This meaning indicates the existence of the Powerful God from many aspects, which we explained in the commentary on His saying, exalted: ﴿Praise belongs to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

[p. 213]

The second: the alternation of the states of night and day, and this is what is meant here by His saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾. This is because light and darkness are two awesome, great armies, and each day one of them overcomes the other at times, and the other overcomes it at other times. This indicates that each of them is overcome and subdued, and there must be a dominant Subduer over both, under whose management and dominion they are, and He is God, glorified and exalted. The meaning of this "wrapping" is that He adds to each of them by the amount that the other loses. As for the meaning of the wrapping of night and day, it is what was narrated in the hadith: "We seek refuge in God from al-hawr after al-kawr," meaning from turning back after advancing. Know that He, glorified and exalted, expressed this meaning by His saying: ﴿He wraps the night over the day﴾, and by His saying: ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and by His saying: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ [al-Hajj: 61], and by His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to remember﴾ [al-Furqan: 62].

The third: considering the states of the stars, especially the sun and the moon, for the sun is the sultan of the day and the moon is the sultan of the night, and most of the interests of this world are bound to them. His saying: ﴿each runs for a specified term﴾: the specified term is the Day of Resurrection. They continue to run until this day, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will be gone. Its parallel is His saying, exalted: ﴿and the sun and the moon are joined﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 9]. The meaning of this subjection is that these spheres revolve like the revolving of a waterwheel (manjanun) in one fixed manner until the Day of Resurrection, and at that time the sky will be folded up like the folding of a scroll for documents.

When God mentioned these three types of celestial proofs, He said: ﴿Unquestionably, He is the Mighty, the Ever-Forgiving.﴾ The meaning is that the creation of these great bodies, although it indicates that He is Mighty, that is, of perfect power, He is also Ever-Forgiving, of great mercy, bounty, and beneficence. For when information about His being of great power produces fear and awe, His being Ever-Forgiving produces abundant mercy, and abundant mercy produces hope and desire. Then He, exalted, followed the mention of the celestial proofs with the mention of proofs drawn from this lower world. He began with mentioning the human being, saying: ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾. The proof of the human being's coming into existence as indicating the God who chooses has been explained many times before.

If it is said: How is it permissible to say ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾ when the mate was created before their creation? They answered this from several aspects:

The first: just as the word "then" (thumma) comes to indicate that one of two events occurred later than the second, so too it comes to indicate that one of two statements is later than the other, like the speaker's saying: "What you did today has reached me, then what you did yesterday was more astonishing," and he also says: "I gave you something today, then what I gave you yesterday was more."

The second: that the sense is "He created you from a soul that was created alone, then its mate was made from it."

The third: God, exalted, brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back like particles (dharr), then after that He created Eve.

Know that when He, exalted, mentioned the argument from His creation of the human being for the existence of the Creator, He mentioned after it the argument from the existence of animals for Him, saying: ﴿and He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock﴾. These are: camels, cattle, sheep, and goats. We have explained how these animals indicate the existence of the Creator in His saying: ﴿and the livestock, He created them for you; in them is warmth﴾ [al-Nahl: 5]. Regarding His saying: ﴿and He sent down for you﴾, there are several aspects:

The first: that God's decree, His determination, and His judgment are described as descending from heaven, because He wrote in the Preserved Tablet every existent that will exist.

The second: that none of the animals lives except by plants, and plants do not subsist except by water and soil, and water descends from heaven. So the sense becomes as if He sent them down.

The third: that He, exalted, created them in Paradise and then sent them down to the earth. His saying: ﴿eight pairs﴾ means a male and a female of the camel, cattle, sheep, and goats. The word "pair" (zawj) is a name for each one that has another with it; when it stands alone, it is a single (fard) of that. He, exalted, said: ﴿and He made from it the two mates, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 39].

[p. 214]

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation﴾, and in this there are discussions:

The first: Hamzah read "ummahatikum" with a kasrah on the alif and the mim; al-Kisa'i read it with a kasrah on the hamzah and a fatḥah on the mim; and the rest read "ummahatikum" with a ḍammah on the alif and a fatḥah on the mim.

The second: when He, exalted, mentioned the creation of people from one person, namely Adam, peace be upon him, He followed it with the creation of livestock. He specifically mentioned them because they are the most noble of animals after the human being. Then, after mentioning these two, He mentioned a state shared between the human being and the livestock, namely their being created in the wombs of their mothers. His saying: ﴿creation after creation﴾ means what God mentioned in His saying: ﴿And We created the human being from an extract of clay﴾ ﴿then We made him a drop in a firm lodging﴾ ﴿then We created the drop a clinging clot, then We created the clot a lump, then We created the lump bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–14]. As for His saying: ﴿in three darknesses﴾, it has been said: the three darknesses are the belly, the womb, and the placenta. It has also been said: the loin, the womb, and the belly. The aspect of argument from these states has been explained in our commentary on His saying: ﴿He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran: 6].

Know that when He, exalted, explained these proofs and described them, He said: ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾. That is, that thing whose wondrous acts you have come to know is God, your Lord. In this verse there is an indication that He, glorified and exalted, is free of parts and limbs, and that He is free of corporeality (jismiyyah) and of being in a place (makaniyyah). This is because when He, exalted, wanted to make His servants know His particular essence, He mentioned only His being the doer of these things. Had He been a body composed of limbs, His definition by those parts and limbs would have been a definition of a thing by the parts of its reality. As for defining Him by His states, acts, and effects, that is a definition of Him by matters external to His essence, and the first definition is more complete than the second. Had that first kind been possible, relying on this second kind would have been a shortcoming and a deficiency, and that is impermissible. So we know that relying on this second kind was only good because the first kind is impossible and impossible to exist. This indicates that He, glorified and exalted, is exalted above corporeality, limbs, and parts.

* * *

If he has dominion, then each of them would be an owner and a capable one, and mutual obstruction would take place between them, as established in His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than God, both would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22], and that is impossible.
