And His saying ﴿from where they did not perceive﴾ means: from the direction they did not reckon, nor did it occur to them that evil would come to them from it, while they were secure; when the punishment came upon them from the direction they had expected to be safe from. Having stated that the punishment came upon them in this world, He also stated that disgrace came upon them, which is humiliation, abasement, and degradation. The benefit of mentioning this qualifier is that complete punishment is that pain be experienced together with degradation and humiliation.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾ [Az-Zumar: 26]. That is: although punishment and disgrace descended upon those people as was mentioned previously, the punishment stored up for them on the Day of Resurrection is greater and more severe than what has befallen them. The purpose of all of this is intimidation and warning. When Allah the Exalted mentioned these abundant benefits and precious gains in these matters, He explained

[Page 240]

Exalted is He; these clarifications have reached the limit of perfection and completeness. So He says: ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they may remember﴾. The purpose is clear. The Mu'tazilah said: the verse indicates that God's acts and rulings are causally motivated (mu'allal), and it also indicates that He wills belief and knowledge from everyone, because His saying ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people﴾ implies causation, and His saying at the end of the verse ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾ also implies causation, and implies that the purpose of setting forth these examples is the desire that remembrance and knowledge be attained. Since these beneficial clarifications and dazzling proofs exist in the Qur'an, the Qur'an is necessarily described with praise and commendation, so He says: ﴿A Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness, that perhaps they may fear God﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Those who hold that the Qur'an is created (muhdath) argued from this verse in several respects:

The first: His saying ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they may remember﴾ indicates that He, exalted is He, mentioned these examples only so that remembrance might occur for them. Whatever is brought for another purpose is created (muhdath), since the eternal (qadim) is that which exists in eternity; and it is impossible to say that He brought it for such-and-such a purpose.

The second: He described it as being "Arabic." It is Arabic only because these words came to indicate these meanings by the convention (wad') and terminology (istilah) of the Arabs, and whatever its occurrence depends upon the conventions and terminologies of the Arabs is created and originated.

The third: He described it as "Qur'an," and "Qur'an" means recitation (qira'ah), and recitation is a verbal noun (masdar), and the masdar is the absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq); so it was an act and an object of the act. The reply: we interpret all these aspects as referring to the letters and sounds, and they are originated and created.

The second issue: al-Zajjaj said: His saying ﴿Arabic﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the meaning is: We set forth for the people in this Qur'an while it is in its Arabic form and its clarity. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative as a term of praise.

The third issue: He, exalted is He, described it with three things:

The first: that it is Qur'an, and the intended meaning is that it is recited in the prayer niches (mihrab) until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

The second: that it is Arabic, and the intended meaning is that it rendered the eloquent and the masters of rhetoric unable to produce its like, as He said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the likeness of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants﴾ [al-Isra': 88].

The third: that it is ﴿without any crookedness﴾, and the intended meaning is its freedom from contradiction, as He said: ﴿Had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾.

As for His saying ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾, the Mu'tazilah hold to it in explaining God's rulings by causes.

There is another discussion regarding this: He, exalted is He, said in the first verse ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾, and in this verse He said ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾. The reason for this is that remembrance precedes fearing God, because when one remembers it, knows it, comprehends its import and grasps its meaning, then fear of God and caution are attained. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verses 22–28 (part 1 of 4):

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord [equal to one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.﴾ ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement: a Book consistent, [and] repeating. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah sends astray – for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿Then is one who will shield with his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is secure]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."﴾ ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.﴾ ﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace in the worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, that they might remember.﴾ ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any deviation, that they might fear Allah.﴾ And in it are issues:

* * *

The first issue: Know that when the Exalted had elaborated on the clear proofs indicating the obligation of turning to the obedience of Allah and the obligation of turning away from this world, He then explained that benefiting from these proofs is not complete except when Allah expands the breasts and illuminates the hearts, so He said: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord﴾.

Know that we elaborated in Surat al-An'am on the explanation of His saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [al-An'am: 125], regarding the explanation of expanding the breast and the explanation of guidance. There is no harm in repeating a little here, so we say: Indeed, He, the Exalted, created the essences of souls differing in their reality. Some of them are good, luminous, noble, inclined toward the divine matters, greatly desiring connection with the spiritual realities, and some of them are base, turbid, vile, inclined toward the corporeal matters. This difference exists in the essences of human souls, and induction indicates that the matter is so. Having known this, we say: The intended meaning of expanding the breast is that intense readiness present in the innate disposition of the soul. When that intense readiness exists, the emergence of that state from potentiality into actuality suffices with the least cause, like sulphur that ignites with the least fire. As for when the soul is far from accepting these holy manifestations and spiritual states, but rather is absorbed in seeking corporeal things, little affected by states suited to divine matters, it becomes hard, turbid, and dark. And whenever the presentation of certain proofs and dazzling demonstrations to it is greater, its hardness and darkness become less.

Having known this principle, we say: As for expanding the breast, it is what we have mentioned. As for the light, it is an expression for guidance and knowledge. If the expansion of the breast does not occur first, the light does not occur second. When what is present is the mere power of the soul, benefit from hearing the proofs does not occur at all, and perhaps hearing the proofs becomes a cause for increased hardness and intense aversion. These are certain foundations that must be known by a person so that he can understand the meanings of these verses. As for the argument of our companions in the issue of compulsion and predestination, and the objections of the opponents to it, it has already preceded there, and Allah knows best.

The second issue: The predicate is omitted, as in His saying: ﴿Or is one who is devoutly obedient...﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. The estimate is: "Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is guided, like one whose heart has been sealed, so he is not guided because of its hardness?" The response is omitted, because the mentioned statement indicates it, namely His saying: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Page 232

The third issue: His saying ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾ contains an objection: the remembrance of Allah is a cause for the attainment of light, guidance, and increased tranquility, as He said: ﴿Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28]. So how does He make it in this verse a cause for the occurrence of hardness of heart? The answer: We say that when the soul is evil in essence, turbid in origin, far from affinity with spiritual things, intensely inclined to bestial natures and blameworthy morals, then hearing the remembrance of Allah increases it in hardness and turbidity. The explanation of this statement by examples: the single agent's actions differ according to the difference of receptacles; the light of the sun blackens the face of the launderer and whitens his cloth, and the heat of the sun softens wax and hardens salt. We see one person state one saying in one assembly, and one finds it pleasant while another finds it disgusting, and this is nothing but what we have mentioned of the difference in the essences of souls and the difference in the states of those souls. «When the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12], and Umar ibn al-Khattab and another man were present there, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached His saying: ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], each of them said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Write it down, for thus it was revealed." Umar increased in faith upon faith, and that man increased in disbelief upon disbelief.» Having known this, it is also not far-fetched that the remembrance of Allah causes light, guidance, and tranquility in pure, spiritual souls, and causes hardness and distance from the truth in wicked, satanic souls.

Having known this, we say: The chief of the medicines that bring about spiritual health, and its head, is the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted. So when it happens to some souls that the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, becomes a cause for the increase of their sickness, the sickness of that soul becomes a sickness whose removal is not hoped for and whose cure is not expected, and it is at the extreme of evil and baseness. For this meaning the Exalted said: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah; those are in manifest error﴾. This is a complete and verified statement.

When the Exalted had explained that, He followed it with what indicates that the Qur'an is a cause for the attainment of light, healing, guidance, and increased tranquility. The purpose of this is to show that since the Qur'an is described with these attributes, yet for that person it became a cause for increased hardness, this indicates that the essence of that soul has reached in baseness and vileness the furthest extremes. So we say: The Exalted described the Qur'an with various kinds of attributes of perfection.

The first attribute: His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾. Concerning it are issues:

The first issue: Those who hold that the Qur'an is created (ḥadith) argued with this verse in several ways:

The first: He, the Exalted, described it as a "ḥadīth" (statement/discourse) in these verses and in other verses, among them His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a statement like it﴾ [al-Tur: 34], and among them His saying: ﴿Then is it this statement that you disdain?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 81]. And a "ḥadīth" must necessarily be newly come into being. They said: Rather, "ḥadīth" is stronger in indicating origination than "ḥādith" (the newly existent), because it is valid to say: "This is a ḥadīth, and it is not ancient," and "This is ancient, and it is not new." Thus it is established that the ḥadīth is that which is recent in its occurrence. The statement was named ḥadīth because it is composed of letters and words, and those letters and words come into being moment by moment and hour by hour. This is the complete exposition of this argument.

As for the second argument, in explaining the people's reasoning: they said: He, the Exalted, described it as having been "sent down" (nazzala), and what is sent down is in a place subject to the disposal of another, and what is so is newly made and originated.

As for the third argument, in explaining the people's reasoning: they said: His saying "the best statement" requires that it be of the same genus as all other statements, just as the saying "Zayd is the best of brothers" requires that Zayd share with those people in the attribute

Page 233

of brotherhood and be of their kind. So it is established that the Qur'an is of the same genus as all other statements, and since all other statements are originated, it must also be that the Qur'an is originated.

As for the fourth argument: they said: He, the Exalted, described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from "kutba," which means gathering together. This indicates that it is a collected and gathering whole, and a place subject to the disposal of one who disposes, and that indicates its being originated. The answer: We say: we apply this argument to the speech composed of letters, sounds, words, and expressions, and that speech, according to us, is originated and created, and Allah knows best.

The second issue: That the Qur'an is "the best statement" is either with respect to its wording or with respect to its meaning.

The first division: that it is the best statement with respect to its wording, and this is in two ways:

The first: that this excellence is on account of eloquence and sublimity.

The second: that it is in accordance with the arrangement of its style, because the Qur'an is not of the genus of poetry, nor of the genus of sermons, nor of the genus of epistles, but is a type that differs from all of them, while every person of sound nature finds it pleasant and delightful.

The second division: that its being the best statement is on account of its meaning, and there are several aspects to this:

The first: that it is a Book free from contradiction, as the Exalted said: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]. A book like this, if free from contradiction, is among the miracles.

The second aspect: its containing many unseen matters concerning the past and the future.

The third aspect: that the sciences present in it are very many.

The regulation of these sciences: we say: The beneficial sciences are what Allah mentioned in His Book in His saying: ﴿And the believers, each believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. This is the best regulation that can be mentioned for the beneficial sciences.

As for the first division, which is belief in Allah, know that it comprises five categories: knowledge of the essence, the attributes, the actions, the rulings, and the names. As for knowledge of the essence, it is to know the existence of Allah, His eternity, and His permanence. As for knowledge of the attributes, it is of two kinds:

One of them: what must be declared free of Him, namely His being a substance, composed of limbs and parts, and His being confined to a space and direction. It must be known that the words indicating transcendence are four: laysa, lam, ma, and la. These four are mentioned in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, to explain transcendence. As for the word "laysa," it is His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. As for "lam," it is His saying: ﴿He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none equal to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 3–4]. As for "ma," it is His saying: ﴿And your Lord is never forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64], ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 35]. As for "la," it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], ﴿He feeds but is not fed﴾ [al-An'am: 14], ﴿He gives protection, and none can give protection against Him﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88], and His saying in thirty-seven places in the Qur'an: ﴿There is no deity except Allah﴾ [al-Saffat: 35].

Page 234

As for the second kind: the attributes that the Qur'an must be described as affirming of Him, the first of them is knowledge of Allah, and knowledge that He is originator and creator. The Exalted said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

The second of them: knowledge that He is capable. The Exalted said at the beginning of Surat al-Qiyamah: ﴿Yes, [We are] able to put together his fingertips﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 4], and He said at the end of this surah: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]... [the text as given in the source has "Is not that [One] capable of giving life to the dead?" [al-Qiyamah: 40]].

The third of them: knowledge that He is knowing. The Exalted said: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ [al-Hashr: 22].

**Fourth:** Knowledge that He is All-Knowing of all things known. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but Him﴾ [Al-An'am: 59], and His saying: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears﴾ [Al-Ra'd: 8].

**Fifth:** Knowledge that He is Living. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He, so call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His﴾ [Ghafir: 65].

**Sixth:** Knowledge that He is Willing. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam﴾ [Al-An'am: 125].

**Seventh:** That He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura: 11], and says: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46].

**Eighth:** That He is Speaking. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Even if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27].

**Ninth:** That He is Commanding. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾ [Ar-Rum: 4].

**Tenth:** That He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the Master. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 3–4].

This is what relates to knowing the attributes that must be affirmed of Him.

As for the third category, which is the Acts: know that the acts are either spirits or bodies. As for spirits, there is no way to comprehend them except for a few, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 31]. As for bodies, they are either the Higher World or the Lower World. The discussion of the Higher World has several aspects:

First: investigation of the conditions of the heavens.

Second: investigation of the conditions of the sun and the moon, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which it follows rapidly, and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54].

Third: investigation of the conditions of lights. Allah says: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [An-Nur: 35], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light﴾ [Yunus: 5].

Fourth: investigation of the conditions of shadows. Allah says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it stationary﴾ [Al-Furqan: 45].

Fifth: the alternation of night and day. Allah says: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾.

Sixth: the benefits of the stars. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea﴾ [Al-An'am: 97].

Seventh: the attributes of Paradise. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Hadid: 21].

Eighth: the attributes of Hell. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate is a portion designated﴾ [Al-Hijr: 44].

Ninth: the attribute of the Throne. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Tenth: the attribute of the Footstool (al-Kursi). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255].

Eleventh: the attribute of the Preserved Tablet and the Pen. As for the Tablet, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a preserved Tablet﴾ [Al-Buruj: 21–22]. As for the Pen, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾ [Al-Qalam: 1–2].

* * *

As for explaining the conditions of the Lower World, the first of them is the earth, and He has described it with many attributes:

The first: that it is a cradle, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He who made the earth a cradle for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53].

The second: that it is a bed (mihad), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have We not made the earth a bed?﴾ [An-Naba': 6].

[p. 235]

The third: that it is a gathering place (kifat), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A gathering place for the living and the dead﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 25–26].

The fourth: that it is tractable (dhalul), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you﴾ [Al-Mulk: 15].

The fifth: that it is a carpet (bisat), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah has made the earth a spread-out carpet for you, that you may traverse therein its broad pathways﴾ [Nuh: 19–20]. The discussion of this is lengthy.

Second: the sea. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ [An-Nahl: 14].

Third: the air and the winds. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [Al-A'raf: 57], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We sent the fertilizing winds﴾ [Al-Hijr: 22].

Fourth: the upper phenomena, such as thunder and lightning. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The thunder exalts [Allah] with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 13], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You see the rain emerging from within it﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 43]. Under this heading falls mention of thunderbolts, rain, and the accumulation of clouds.

Fifth: the conditions of trees and fruits, and their kinds and varieties.

Sixth: the conditions of animals. Allah says: ﴿And He spread throughout it every kind of creature﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164], and He says: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you﴾ [An-Nahl: 5].

Seventh: the wonders of the creation of man at the beginning of his creation. He says: ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12].

Eighth: the wonders in his hearing, sight, tongue, intellect, and understanding.

Ninth: the histories of the prophets and kings, and the conditions of people from the beginning of the creation of the world until the final Hour of the Resurrection.

Tenth: mention of the conditions of people at death and after death, the manner of resurrection and the Last Day, and an explanation of the conditions of the blessed and the wretched. We have indicated ten kinds of knowledge in the world of the heavens and ten others in the world of the elements, and the Qur'an comprises the explanation of these kinds of sublime and elevated knowledge.

As for the fourth category, which is the explanation of the rulings of Allah the Exalted and His obligations: we say that these obligations either pertain to the actions of the hearts or to the actions of the limbs.

As for the first category: it is what is called the science of ethics (ʿilm al-akhlaq), and the clarification of distinguishing virtuous morals from corrupt morals. The Qur'an comprises everything that is necessary in this domain. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality, bad conduct, and oppression﴾ [An-Nahl: 90], and He says: ﴿Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [Al-A'raf: 199].

As for the second: it is the obligations that take effect in the actions of the limbs, and this is what is called the science of jurisprudence (ʿilm al-fiqh). The Qur'an comprises the totality of the principles of this science in the most complete manner.

As for the fifth category: knowledge of the names of Allah the Exalted. It is mentioned in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 180]. All of this relates to knowing Allah.

As for the second category of the principles that are considered in faith: affirming the angels, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the believers, each believed in Allah and His angels﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. The Qur'an comprises an explanation of their attributes, sometimes in summary and sometimes in detail. As for the summary, it is His saying: ﴿and His angels﴾. As for the detail, some of it indicates that they are messengers of Allah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ [Fatir: 1]. Some of it indicates that they govern this world. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then by those who distribute by command﴾, ﴿then by those who arrange affairs﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 5], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And by those who line up in rows﴾ [As-Saffat: 1]. Some of it concerns the bearers of the Throne. He says: ﴿And above them, on that Day, eight will carry the Throne of your Lord﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 17]. Some of it concerns those who surround the Throne. He says: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75]. Some of it concerns the keepers of Hell. He says: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾ [At-Tahrim: 6]. Some of it concerns the Noble Recorders. He says: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording﴾ [Al-Infitar: 10–11]. Some of it concerns the successive angels. He says: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]. The conditions of jinn and devils are often connected with the conditions of the angels.

As for the third category of the principles considered in faith: knowledge of the books. The Qur'an comprises an explanation of the conditions of the scripture of Adam, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 37]. Some of it concerns the scrolls of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124]. Some of it concerns the conditions of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms.

As for the fourth category of the principles considered in faith: knowledge of the messengers. Allah the Exalted has explained the conditions of some and left the conditions of the rest unspecified. He says: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir: 78].

The fifth category: what relates to the conditions of the accountable persons, and it is of two types:

The first: that they acknowledge the obligation of these duties upon them. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285].

The second: that they acknowledge that shortcomings have proceeded from them in those actions, and then they seek forgiveness. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿"Your forgiveness, our Lord"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. Then, since the measures of perceiving shortcoming in the stations of servanthood vary according to the unveilings in contemplating the majesty of Lordship, the unveilings of the shortcoming of servanthood are greater, and the saying ﴿"Your forgiveness, our Lord"﴾ is greater.

The sixth category: knowledge of the return, the resurrection, and the Last Day. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And to You is the final return﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. This is the indication toward knowing the important matters in seeking religion. The Qur'an is an ocean without end in establishing these matters, defining them, and explaining them. You will not find in the eastern and western lands a book that comprises the totality of these sciences as the Qur'an does. Whoever reflects on this commentary will know that we have not mentioned from the oceans of the Qur'an's virtues except a drop. Since the matter stands on this totality, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has indeed praised the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾. And Allah knows best.

The second attribute of the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿A Book resembling itself [mutashabihan]﴾. As for "Book," we have explained it in His saying: ﴿This is the Book about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 2]. As for its being mutashabih (resembling, uniform in its parts), know that this verse indicates that the whole Qur'an is mutashabih, while His saying: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are muhkam (firm), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are mutashabih (ambiguous)﴾ [Al-'Imran: 7] indicates that some of it is mutashabih and not all of it.

As for its being entirely mutashabih, as in this verse, Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is that some of it resembles other parts of it. I say: this resemblance occurs in several respects:

First: when an eloquent writer writes a long book, some of his words are eloquent and some are not eloquent. The Qur'an differs from this, for it is eloquent with perfect eloquence in all its parts.

Second: when an eloquent person writes a book about an event with eloquent words, if he then writes another book about a different event, the general likelihood is that his speech in the second book will differ from his speech in the first. Allah the Exalted has related the story of Musa, peace be upon him, in many places in the Qur'an, and all of them are equal and similar in eloquence.

Third: all of its verses and clarifications strengthen one another and confirm one another.

Fourth: these many kinds of knowledge that we have enumerated are similar and shared in that their purpose altogether is the call to religion and the affirmation of Allah's greatness. For this reason, you will not see any story from the stories except that its outcome is the purpose we have mentioned. This is what is meant by its being mutashabih. And Allah is the Guide.

The third attribute of the Qur'an is that it is *mathani* (repeated, paired). We have elaborated on this term at His saying: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the mathani﴾ [Al-Hijr: 87]. In summary, most of the things mentioned occur in pairs, such as: command and prohibition, general and specific, concise and detailed, the conditions of the heavens and the earth, Paradise and Hell, darkness and light, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, the angels and the devils, the Throne and the Footstool, promise and threat, hope and fear. The purpose of this is to show that everything other than the Truth is paired, and to indicate that everything is tested with its opposite and counterpart, and that the One, the Single, the Real is Allah, glorified is He.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 39, verses 22–28 (part 3 of 4):**

The fourth attribute of the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar: 23]. On this verse there are several issues.

* * *

**The first issue:** The meaning of ﴿shiver from it﴾ is that their skins are seized by *qush'ariyyah* (a shivering or bristling of the skin), which is a change that occurs in the human skin out of dread and fear. The exegetes (*mufassirun*) said: the meaning is that when they hear verses of mercy and kindness, joy comes to them, and so their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. I say: the verifying scholars among the knowers of God said: "Travellers at the beginning of the majesty of Allah, if they look upon the world of majesty, they are overwhelmed, and if a trace of the world of beauty appears to them, they come alive." It is necessary for us to mention in this matter further explanation and elaboration, so we say: when a person reflects upon the proofs indicating that Allah must be declared free of being confined to a space or direction, his skin shivers here, because establishing an existent that is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither joined to the world nor separate from it, is something difficult to conceive; here the skins shiver. But when he reflects upon the proofs indicating that He must be one, a single unity, and it is established that everything confined to a space is divisible, here his skin and heart soften to the remembrance of Allah.

Also, if he wishes his intellect to encompass the meaning of *azal* (pre-eternity), so that in his mind he advances by a thousand thousand years, then advances again by a thousand thousand years for each moment of that period, and keeps contriving and advancing and imagining in the mind, then when he strains and goes deep and thinks he has grasped the meaning of *azal*, the intellect says: "This is nothing, for everything I have grasped within me is finite, and *azal* is the existence that precedes this finite duration." Here the intellect is bewildered and the skin shivers. But if he sets aside this consideration and says: "Here there is an existent, and the existent is either necessary or contingent; if it is necessary, it is always exempt from first and last; and if it is contingent, it needs the necessary, so it is eternal and everlasting." When the intellect considers this, it understands the meaning of eternity, and here his skin and heart soften to the remembrance of Allah. Thus it is established that the two states mentioned in the verse are not restricted to hearing a verse of punishment and a verse of mercy; rather that is the first of these stations, and after it there are stations without limit or end in the occurrence of those two states.

**The second issue:** Al-Wahidi narrated in *al-Basit* from Qatadah that he said: "The Qur'an indicates that the friends of Allah are described as follows: at times of unveilings and direct witnessings, sometimes their skins shiver and sometimes their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah, and it does not say that their intellects depart or that their limbs convulse. This indicates that if those states were to occur, they would be from Satan." I say: here is another investigation. Shaykh Abu Hamid al-Ghazali raised an issue in *Ihya' Ulum al-Din*, namely that we see many people who experience intense and complete ecstasy (*wajd*) upon hearing verses that describe union and separation, while upon hearing the verses of the Qur'an nothing of these states appears in them. Then he accepted this matter and gave excuses for it in many ways. I say: I was created deprived of this meaning, for whenever I reflect upon the secrets of the Qur'an, my skin shivers, my hair stands on end, and astonishment and awe enter my heart; and whenever I hear those poems, levity overcomes me and I find no effect of them in myself at all. I think the straight path and the upright method is this, and its explanation is in several aspects:

*First:* Those poems are words containing union, separation, hatred and love, which befit created beings; ascribing them to Allah the Exalted is disbelief. As for moving from those states to meanings fitting the majesty of Allah, only the firmly grounded scholars (*al-'ulama' al-rasikhun fi al-'ilm*) reach them. The meanings contained in the Qur'an are states fitting the majesty of Allah, so whoever comes to know them, the awe in his heart is greatly magnified, for whoever has the light of faith must have his agitation greatly increased upon hearing His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [Al-An'am: 59], to the end of the verse.

*Second:* I heard some shaykhs say: just as speech has an effect, so too the utterance of that speech from a specific speaker has an effect, for the strength of the speaker's soul helps the speech to penetrate the spirit. The speaker in the Qur'an here is Allah, through Jibril, conveying through the infallible Messenger; while the speaker there is a lying poet, filled with lust and calling to immorality.

*Third:* The core of the Qur'an is the call to the truth. He the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52–53]. As for poetry, its core is falsehood. He the Exalted said: ﴿And the poets—the deviators follow them. Have you not seen that they wander in every valley? And that they say what they do not do﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 224–226]. These three aspects are clear distinctions. As for what relates to the inner experience of the soul, each person only reports what he finds in his own soul, and what I have found of the soul and intellect is what I have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

**The third issue:** Regarding the remaining difficulties of this verse, we mention them in the form of questions and answers.

**Question 1:** What is the morphology of the word *qushʿarīrah*? Answer: The author of *al-Kashshaf* (Zamakhshari's commentary) said: its structure is from the letters of *taqashshu'* (the peeling away of dry hide), with a fourth letter added to it, which is the *ra'*, so that it becomes quadriliteral and indicates an additional meaning. It is said: "His skin shivered from fear and his hair stood on end," and this is an image for the intensity of fear.

**Question 2:** Why did He say ﴿their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾, and what is the reason for its construction with the preposition *ila* (to)? Answer: The estimated meaning is: their skins and hearts soften at the moment of their arrival into the presence of Allah, and this is not perceived by sense-perception.

**Question 3:** Why did He say "to the remembrance of Allah" and not "to the remembrance of the mercy of Allah"? Answer: Whoever loves Allah for the sake of His mercy has not truly loved Allah; he has only loved something else. But whoever loves Allah for nothing other than Him, this is the true lover, and this is the lofty rank. For this reason He did not say "to the remembrance of the mercy of Allah," but said "to the remembrance of Allah." Allah the Exalted explained this meaning in His saying: ﴿So whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [Al-An'am: 125], and in His saying: ﴿Surely by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 28]. Also, He said to the community of Musa: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 40], and He also said to the community of Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 152].

**Question 4:** Why did He mention only the shivering of the skins in the context of fear, but the softening of both skins and hearts together in the context of hope? Answer: Because the unveiling (*mukashafah*) in the station of hope is more perfect than in the station of fear, since good is sought for its own sake, while evil is sought only incidentally, and the locus of unveilings is the hearts and spirits. And Allah knows best.

Then, when He the Exalted had described the Qur'an with these attributes, He said: ﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides by it whom He wills, and whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [Az-Zumar: 23]. His saying ﴿That﴾ refers to the Book, which is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills among His servants, and He is the One who first expanded his breast to accept this guidance. ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray﴾, that is, whoever He makes his heart hard, dark, dull of understanding, and incompatible with accepting this guidance, ﴿for him there is no guide.﴾ The argument of our companions (the Ash'aris) from this verse, the questions of the Mu'tazila and the answers of our companions, are the very same as what preceded in His saying: ﴿So whoever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [Al-An'am: 125].

* * *

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿Is one who will shield his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is secure]?﴾ know that He the Exalted passed a judgment upon those whose hearts are hardened, one judgment in this world and another in the Hereafter. As for their judgment in this world, it is complete misguidance, as He said: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. As for their judgment in the Hereafter, it is severe punishment, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Is one who will shield his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Its explanation: the noblest of the limbs is the face, for it is the seat of beauty and radiance, and it is also the citadel of the senses; people are distinguished from one another by means of the face, and the effect of happiness and wretchedness appears only in the face. He the Exalted said: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, joyful; and faces that Day will be upon them dust, darkness covering them; those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 38–42]. It is said to the foremost of a people: "O face of the Arabs"; and it is said of a path that indicates the true condition of a thing: "The face of such-and-such is such-and-such." Thus it is established from what we have mentioned that the noblest of the limbs is the face. So when a person falls into some kind of punishment, he makes his hand a shield for his face and a ransom for it. Knowing this, we say: if the one able to protect himself makes everything other than the face a ransom for the face, then it is rightly fitting to make protecting oneself "with the face" a metaphor for inability to protect oneself. A parallel to this is the saying of al-Nabigha:

*"And there is no fault in them, except that their swords are notched from the clashing of battalions."*

That is: there is no fault in them except this, and this is not a fault; so there is no fault in them in any respect whatsoever. Likewise here: they cannot protect themselves in any way except with the face, and this is not protection; so they have no ability at all to protect themselves. It is also said: the one thrown into the Fire is thrown with his hands chained to his neck, and he cannot prepare to protect himself from the Fire except with his face. Knowing this, we say: its answer is omitted, and its estimated meaning is: "Is one who shields his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection like one who is secure from the punishment?" So the predicate has been omitted, as it is omitted in its parallels. And *su' al-'adhab* (the worst of the punishment) means its severity.

* * *

Then He the Exalted said: ﴿And it will be said to the wrongdoers: Taste what you used to earn﴾ [Az-Zumar: 24]. When Allah had explained the manner of punishment for those whose hearts are hardened in the Hereafter, He also explained the manner of their falling into punishment in this world. He said: ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive﴾ [Az-Zumar: 25]. This is an alert concerning the condition of these people, for the *fa'* in His saying ﴿and the punishment came upon them﴾ indicates that the punishment came upon them only because of denial. So if denial exists here, the occurrence of punishment necessarily follows, by inferring the effect from its cause. And His saying ﴿from where they did not perceive﴾ means: from the direction they did not reckon, nor did it occur to them that evil would come to them from it, while they were secure; when the punishment came upon them from the direction they had expected to be safe from. Having stated that the punishment came upon them in this world, He also stated that disgrace came upon them, which is humiliation, abasement, and degradation. The benefit of mentioning this qualifier is that complete punishment is that pain be experienced together with degradation and humiliation.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew﴾ [Az-Zumar: 26]. That is: although punishment and disgrace descended upon those people as was mentioned previously, the punishment stored up for them on the Day of Resurrection is greater and more severe than what has befallen them. The purpose of all of this is intimidation and warning. When Allah the Exalted mentioned these abundant benefits and precious gains in these matters, He explained

[Page 240]

Exalted is He; these clarifications have reached the limit of perfection and completeness. So He says: ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they may remember﴾. The purpose is clear. The Mu'tazilah said: the verse indicates that God's acts and rulings are causally motivated (mu'allal), and it also indicates that He wills belief and knowledge from everyone, because His saying ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people﴾ implies causation, and His saying at the end of the verse ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾ also implies causation, and implies that the purpose of setting forth these examples is the desire that remembrance and knowledge be attained. Since these beneficial clarifications and dazzling proofs exist in the Qur'an, the Qur'an is necessarily described with praise and commendation, so He says: ﴿A Qur'an in Arabic, without any crookedness, that perhaps they may fear God﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Those who hold that the Qur'an is created (muhdath) argued from this verse in several respects:

The first: His saying ﴿And We have certainly set forth for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, that perhaps they may remember﴾ indicates that He, exalted is He, mentioned these examples only so that remembrance might occur for them. Whatever is brought for another purpose is created (muhdath), since the eternal (qadim) is that which exists in eternity; and it is impossible to say that He brought it for such-and-such a purpose.

The second: He described it as being "Arabic." It is Arabic only because these words came to indicate these meanings by the convention (wad') and terminology (istilah) of the Arabs, and whatever its occurrence depends upon the conventions and terminologies of the Arabs is created and originated.

The third: He described it as "Qur'an," and "Qur'an" means recitation (qira'ah), and recitation is a verbal noun (masdar), and the masdar is the absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq); so it was an act and an object of the act. The reply: we interpret all these aspects as referring to the letters and sounds, and they are originated and created.

The second issue: al-Zajjaj said: His saying ﴿Arabic﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and the meaning is: We set forth for the people in this Qur'an while it is in its Arabic form and its clarity. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative as a term of praise.

The third issue: He, exalted is He, described it with three things:

The first: that it is Qur'an, and the intended meaning is that it is recited in the prayer niches (mihrab) until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

The second: that it is Arabic, and the intended meaning is that it rendered the eloquent and the masters of rhetoric unable to produce its like, as He said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the likeness of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants﴾ [al-Isra': 88].

The third: that it is ﴿without any crookedness﴾, and the intended meaning is its freedom from contradiction, as He said: ﴿Had it been from other than God, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾.

As for His saying ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾, the Mu'tazilah hold to it in explaining God's rulings by causes.

There is another discussion regarding this: He, exalted is He, said in the first verse ﴿that perhaps they may remember﴾, and in this verse He said ﴿that perhaps they may fear God﴾. The reason for this is that remembrance precedes fearing God, because when one remembers it, knows it, comprehends its import and grasps its meaning, then fear of God and caution are attained. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verses 22–28 (part 1 of 4):

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord [equal to one whose heart is hardened]? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.﴾ ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement: a Book consistent, [and] repeating. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah sends astray – for him there is no guide.﴾ ﴿Then is one who will shield with his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is secure]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."﴾ ﴿Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.﴾ ﴿So Allah made them taste disgrace in the worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, that they might remember.﴾ ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any deviation, that they might fear Allah.﴾ And in it are issues:

* * *

The first issue: Know that when the Exalted had elaborated on the clear proofs indicating the obligation of turning to the obedience of Allah and the obligation of turning away from this world, He then explained that benefiting from these proofs is not complete except when Allah expands the breasts and illuminates the hearts, so He said: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord﴾.

Know that we elaborated in Surat al-An'am on the explanation of His saying: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [al-An'am: 125], regarding the explanation of expanding the breast and the explanation of guidance. There is no harm in repeating a little here, so we say: Indeed, He, the Exalted, created the essences of souls differing in their reality. Some of them are good, luminous, noble, inclined toward the divine matters, greatly desiring connection with the spiritual realities, and some of them are base, turbid, vile, inclined toward the corporeal matters. This difference exists in the essences of human souls, and induction indicates that the matter is so. Having known this, we say: The intended meaning of expanding the breast is that intense readiness present in the innate disposition of the soul. When that intense readiness exists, the emergence of that state from potentiality into actuality suffices with the least cause, like sulphur that ignites with the least fire. As for when the soul is far from accepting these holy manifestations and spiritual states, but rather is absorbed in seeking corporeal things, little affected by states suited to divine matters, it becomes hard, turbid, and dark. And whenever the presentation of certain proofs and dazzling demonstrations to it is greater, its hardness and darkness become less.

Having known this principle, we say: As for expanding the breast, it is what we have mentioned. As for the light, it is an expression for guidance and knowledge. If the expansion of the breast does not occur first, the light does not occur second. When what is present is the mere power of the soul, benefit from hearing the proofs does not occur at all, and perhaps hearing the proofs becomes a cause for increased hardness and intense aversion. These are certain foundations that must be known by a person so that he can understand the meanings of these verses. As for the argument of our companions in the issue of compulsion and predestination, and the objections of the opponents to it, it has already preceded there, and Allah knows best.

The second issue: The predicate is omitted, as in His saying: ﴿Or is one who is devoutly obedient...﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]. The estimate is: "Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is guided, like one whose heart has been sealed, so he is not guided because of its hardness?" The response is omitted, because the mentioned statement indicates it, namely His saying: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Page 232

The third issue: His saying ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾ contains an objection: the remembrance of Allah is a cause for the attainment of light, guidance, and increased tranquility, as He said: ﴿Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28]. So how does He make it in this verse a cause for the occurrence of hardness of heart? The answer: We say that when the soul is evil in essence, turbid in origin, far from affinity with spiritual things, intensely inclined to bestial natures and blameworthy morals, then hearing the remembrance of Allah increases it in hardness and turbidity. The explanation of this statement by examples: the single agent's actions differ according to the difference of receptacles; the light of the sun blackens the face of the launderer and whitens his cloth, and the heat of the sun softens wax and hardens salt. We see one person state one saying in one assembly, and one finds it pleasant while another finds it disgusting, and this is nothing but what we have mentioned of the difference in the essences of souls and the difference in the states of those souls. «When the saying of the Exalted was revealed: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12], and Umar ibn al-Khattab and another man were present there, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached His saying: ﴿Then We produced him as another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], each of them said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Write it down, for thus it was revealed." Umar increased in faith upon faith, and that man increased in disbelief upon disbelief.» Having known this, it is also not far-fetched that the remembrance of Allah causes light, guidance, and tranquility in pure, spiritual souls, and causes hardness and distance from the truth in wicked, satanic souls.

Having known this, we say: The chief of the medicines that bring about spiritual health, and its head, is the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted. So when it happens to some souls that the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, becomes a cause for the increase of their sickness, the sickness of that soul becomes a sickness whose removal is not hoped for and whose cure is not expected, and it is at the extreme of evil and baseness. For this meaning the Exalted said: ﴿Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah; those are in manifest error﴾. This is a complete and verified statement.

When the Exalted had explained that, He followed it with what indicates that the Qur'an is a cause for the attainment of light, healing, guidance, and increased tranquility. The purpose of this is to show that since the Qur'an is described with these attributes, yet for that person it became a cause for increased hardness, this indicates that the essence of that soul has reached in baseness and vileness the furthest extremes. So we say: The Exalted described the Qur'an with various kinds of attributes of perfection.

The first attribute: His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾. Concerning it are issues:

The first issue: Those who hold that the Qur'an is created (ḥadith) argued with this verse in several ways:

The first: He, the Exalted, described it as a "ḥadīth" (statement/discourse) in these verses and in other verses, among them His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a statement like it﴾ [al-Tur: 34], and among them His saying: ﴿Then is it this statement that you disdain?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 81]. And a "ḥadīth" must necessarily be newly come into being. They said: Rather, "ḥadīth" is stronger in indicating origination than "ḥādith" (the newly existent), because it is valid to say: "This is a ḥadīth, and it is not ancient," and "This is ancient, and it is not new." Thus it is established that the ḥadīth is that which is recent in its occurrence. The statement was named ḥadīth because it is composed of letters and words, and those letters and words come into being moment by moment and hour by hour. This is the complete exposition of this argument.

As for the second argument, in explaining the people's reasoning: they said: He, the Exalted, described it as having been "sent down" (nazzala), and what is sent down is in a place subject to the disposal of another, and what is so is newly made and originated.

As for the third argument, in explaining the people's reasoning: they said: His saying "the best statement" requires that it be of the same genus as all other statements, just as the saying "Zayd is the best of brothers" requires that Zayd share with those people in the attribute

Page 233

of brotherhood and be of their kind. So it is established that the Qur'an is of the same genus as all other statements, and since all other statements are originated, it must also be that the Qur'an is originated.

As for the fourth argument: they said: He, the Exalted, described it as a "Book" (kitāb), and "kitāb" is derived from "kutba," which means gathering together. This indicates that it is a collected and gathering whole, and a place subject to the disposal of one who disposes, and that indicates its being originated. The answer: We say: we apply this argument to the speech composed of letters, sounds, words, and expressions, and that speech, according to us, is originated and created, and Allah knows best.

The second issue: That the Qur'an is "the best statement" is either with respect to its wording or with respect to its meaning.

The first division: that it is the best statement with respect to its wording, and this is in two ways:

The first: that this excellence is on account of eloquence and sublimity.

The second: that it is in accordance with the arrangement of its style, because the Qur'an is not of the genus of poetry, nor of the genus of sermons, nor of the genus of epistles, but is a type that differs from all of them, while every person of sound nature finds it pleasant and delightful.

The second division: that its being the best statement is on account of its meaning, and there are several aspects to this:

The first: that it is a Book free from contradiction, as the Exalted said: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]. A book like this, if free from contradiction, is among the miracles.

The second aspect: its containing many unseen matters concerning the past and the future.

The third aspect: that the sciences present in it are very many.

The regulation of these sciences: we say: The beneficial sciences are what Allah mentioned in His Book in His saying: ﴿And the believers, each believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285]. This is the best regulation that can be mentioned for the beneficial sciences.

As for the first division, which is belief in Allah, know that it comprises five categories: knowledge of the essence, the attributes, the actions, the rulings, and the names. As for knowledge of the essence, it is to know the existence of Allah, His eternity, and His permanence. As for knowledge of the attributes, it is of two kinds:

One of them: what must be declared free of Him, namely His being a substance, composed of limbs and parts, and His being confined to a space and direction. It must be known that the words indicating transcendence are four: laysa, lam, ma, and la. These four are mentioned in the Book of Allah, the Exalted, to explain transcendence. As for the word "laysa," it is His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11]. As for "lam," it is His saying: ﴿He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none equal to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 3–4]. As for "ma," it is His saying: ﴿And your Lord is never forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64], ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 35]. As for "la," it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], ﴿He feeds but is not fed﴾ [al-An'am: 14], ﴿He gives protection, and none can give protection against Him﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 88], and His saying in thirty-seven places in the Qur'an: ﴿There is no deity except Allah﴾ [al-Saffat: 35].

Page 234

As for the second kind: the attributes that the Qur'an must be described as affirming of Him, the first of them is knowledge of Allah, and knowledge that He is originator and creator. The Exalted said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

The second of them: knowledge that He is capable. The Exalted said at the beginning of Surat al-Qiyamah: ﴿Yes, [We are] able to put together his fingertips﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 4], and He said at the end of this surah: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]... [the text as given in the source has "Is not that [One] capable of giving life to the dead?" [al-Qiyamah: 40]].

The third of them: knowledge that He is knowing. The Exalted said: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ [al-Hashr: 22].

**Fourth:** Knowledge that He is All-Knowing of all things known. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but Him﴾ [Al-An'am: 59], and His saying: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears﴾ [Al-Ra'd: 8].

**Fifth:** Knowledge that He is Living. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He is the Living; there is no god but He, so call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His﴾ [Ghafir: 65].

**Sixth:** Knowledge that He is Willing. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam﴾ [Al-An'am: 125].

**Seventh:** That He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura: 11], and says: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46].

**Eighth:** That He is Speaking. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Even if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman: 27].

**Ninth:** That He is Commanding. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿To Allah belongs the command before and after﴾ [Ar-Rum: 4].

**Tenth:** That He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the Master. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, Master of the Day of Recompense﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 3–4].

This is what relates to knowing the attributes that must be affirmed of Him.

As for the third category, which is the Acts: know that the acts are either spirits or bodies. As for spirits, there is no way to comprehend them except for a few, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 31]. As for bodies, they are either the Higher World or the Lower World. The discussion of the Higher World has several aspects:

First: investigation of the conditions of the heavens.

Second: investigation of the conditions of the sun and the moon, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which it follows rapidly, and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54].

Third: investigation of the conditions of lights. Allah says: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [An-Nur: 35], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light﴾ [Yunus: 5].

Fourth: investigation of the conditions of shadows. Allah says: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow? Had He willed, He would have made it stationary﴾ [Al-Furqan: 45].

Fifth: the alternation of night and day. Allah says: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾.

Sixth: the benefits of the stars. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea﴾ [Al-An'am: 97].

Seventh: the attributes of Paradise. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Hadid: 21].

Eighth: the attributes of Hell. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate is a portion designated﴾ [Al-Hijr: 44].

Ninth: the attribute of the Throne. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

Tenth: the attribute of the Footstool (al-Kursi). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255].

Eleventh: the attribute of the Preserved Tablet and the Pen. As for the Tablet, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a preserved Tablet﴾ [Al-Buruj: 21–22]. As for the Pen, the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾ [Al-Qalam: 1–2].

* * *

As for explaining the conditions of the Lower World, the first of them is the earth, and He has described it with many attributes:

The first: that it is a cradle, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He who made the earth a cradle for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 53].

The second: that it is a bed (mihad), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have We not made the earth a bed?﴾ [An-Naba': 6].

[p. 235]

The third: that it is a gathering place (kifat), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿A gathering place for the living and the dead﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 25–26].

The fourth: that it is tractable (dhalul), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you﴾ [Al-Mulk: 15].

The fifth: that it is a carpet (bisat), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah has made the earth a spread-out carpet for you, that you may traverse therein its broad pathways﴾ [Nuh: 19–20]. The discussion of this is lengthy.

Second: the sea. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ [An-Nahl: 14].

Third: the air and the winds. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [Al-A'raf: 57], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We sent the fertilizing winds﴾ [Al-Hijr: 22].

Fourth: the upper phenomena, such as thunder and lightning. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The thunder exalts [Allah] with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 13], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You see the rain emerging from within it﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 43]. Under this heading falls mention of thunderbolts, rain, and the accumulation of clouds.

Fifth: the conditions of trees and fruits, and their kinds and varieties.

Sixth: the conditions of animals. Allah says: ﴿And He spread throughout it every kind of creature﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 164], and He says: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you﴾ [An-Nahl: 5].

Seventh: the wonders of the creation of man at the beginning of his creation. He says: ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12].

Eighth: the wonders in his hearing, sight, tongue, intellect, and understanding.

Ninth: the histories of the prophets and kings, and the conditions of people from the beginning of the creation of the world until the final Hour of the Resurrection.

Tenth: mention of the conditions of people at death and after death, the manner of resurrection and the Last Day, and an explanation of the conditions of the blessed and the wretched. We have indicated ten kinds of knowledge in the world of the heavens and ten others in the world of the elements, and the Qur'an comprises the explanation of these kinds of sublime and elevated knowledge.

As for the fourth category, which is the explanation of the rulings of Allah the Exalted and His obligations: we say that these obligations either pertain to the actions of the hearts or to the actions of the limbs.

As for the first category: it is what is called the science of ethics (ʿilm al-akhlaq), and the clarification of distinguishing virtuous morals from corrupt morals. The Qur'an comprises everything that is necessary in this domain. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality, bad conduct, and oppression﴾ [An-Nahl: 90], and He says: ﴿Take what is given freely, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [Al-A'raf: 199].

As for the second: it is the obligations that take effect in the actions of the limbs, and this is what is called the science of jurisprudence (ʿilm al-fiqh). The Qur'an comprises the totality of the principles of this science in the most complete manner.

As for the fifth category: knowledge of the names of Allah the Exalted. It is mentioned in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so invoke Him by them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 180]. All of this relates to knowing Allah.

As for the second category of the principles that are considered in faith: affirming the angels, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the believers, each believed in Allah and His angels﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. The Qur'an comprises an explanation of their attributes, sometimes in summary and sometimes in detail. As for the summary, it is His saying: ﴿and His angels﴾. As for the detail, some of it indicates that they are messengers of Allah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ [Fatir: 1]. Some of it indicates that they govern this world. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then by those who distribute by command﴾, ﴿then by those who arrange affairs﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 5], and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And by those who line up in rows﴾ [As-Saffat: 1]. Some of it concerns the bearers of the Throne. He says: ﴿And above them, on that Day, eight will carry the Throne of your Lord﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 17]. Some of it concerns those who surround the Throne. He says: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ [Az-Zumar: 75]. Some of it concerns the keepers of Hell. He says: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾ [At-Tahrim: 6]. Some of it concerns the Noble Recorders. He says: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording﴾ [Al-Infitar: 10–11]. Some of it concerns the successive angels. He says: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11]. The conditions of jinn and devils are often connected with the conditions of the angels.

As for the third category of the principles considered in faith: knowledge of the books. The Qur'an comprises an explanation of the conditions of the scripture of Adam, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 37]. Some of it concerns the scrolls of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tried by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 124]. Some of it concerns the conditions of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms.

As for the fourth category of the principles considered in faith: knowledge of the messengers. Allah the Exalted has explained the conditions of some and left the conditions of the rest unspecified. He says: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir: 78].

The fifth category: what relates to the conditions of the accountable persons, and it is of two types:

The first: that they acknowledge the obligation of these duties upon them. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285].

The second: that they acknowledge that shortcomings have proceeded from them in those actions, and then they seek forgiveness. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿"Your forgiveness, our Lord"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. Then, since the measures of perceiving shortcoming in the stations of servanthood vary according to the unveilings in contemplating the majesty of Lordship, the unveilings of the shortcoming of servanthood are greater, and the saying ﴿"Your forgiveness, our Lord"﴾ is greater.

The sixth category: knowledge of the return, the resurrection, and the Last Day. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And to You is the final return﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 285]. This is the indication toward knowing the important matters in seeking religion. The Qur'an is an ocean without end in establishing these matters, defining them, and explaining them. You will not find in the eastern and western lands a book that comprises the totality of these sciences as the Qur'an does. Whoever reflects on this commentary will know that we have not mentioned from the oceans of the Qur'an's virtues except a drop. Since the matter stands on this totality, Allah the Mighty and Majestic has indeed praised the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾. And Allah knows best.

The second attribute of the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿A Book resembling itself [mutashabihan]﴾. As for "Book," we have explained it in His saying: ﴿This is the Book about which there is no doubt﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 2]. As for its being mutashabih (resembling, uniform in its parts), know that this verse indicates that the whole Qur'an is mutashabih, while His saying: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are muhkam (firm), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are mutashabih (ambiguous)﴾ [Al-'Imran: 7] indicates that some of it is mutashabih and not all of it.

As for its being entirely mutashabih, as in this verse, Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is that some of it resembles other parts of it. I say: this resemblance occurs in several respects:

First: when an eloquent writer writes a long book, some of his words are eloquent and some are not eloquent. The Qur'an differs from this, for it is eloquent with perfect eloquence in all its parts.

Second: when an eloquent person writes a book about an event with eloquent words, if he then writes another book about a different event, the general likelihood is that his speech in the second book will differ from his speech in the first. Allah the Exalted has related the story of Musa, peace be upon him, in many places in the Qur'an, and all of them are equal and similar in eloquence.

Third: all of its verses and clarifications strengthen one another and confirm one another.

Fourth: these many kinds of knowledge that we have enumerated are similar and shared in that their purpose altogether is the call to religion and the affirmation of Allah's greatness. For this reason, you will not see any story from the stories except that its outcome is the purpose we have mentioned. This is what is meant by its being mutashabih. And Allah is the Guide.

The third attribute of the Qur'an is that it is *mathani* (repeated, paired). We have elaborated on this term at His saying: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the mathani﴾ [Al-Hijr: 87]. In summary, most of the things mentioned occur in pairs, such as: command and prohibition, general and specific, concise and detailed, the conditions of the heavens and the earth, Paradise and Hell, darkness and light, the Preserved Tablet and the Pen, the angels and the devils, the Throne and the Footstool, promise and threat, hope and fear. The purpose of this is to show that everything other than the Truth is paired, and to indicate that everything is tested with its opposite and counterpart, and that the One, the Single, the Real is Allah, glorified is He.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 39, verses 22–28 (part 3 of 4):**

The fourth attribute of the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar: 23]. On this verse there are several issues.

* * *

**The first issue:** The meaning of ﴿shiver from it﴾ is that their skins are seized by *qush'ariyyah* (a shivering or bristling of the skin), which is a change that occurs in the human skin out of dread and fear. The exegetes (*mufassirun*) said: the meaning is that when they hear verses of mercy and kindness, joy comes to them, and so their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. I say: the verifying scholars among the knowers of God said: "Travellers at the beginning of the majesty of Allah, if they look upon the world of majesty, they are overwhelmed, and if a trace of the world of beauty appears to them, they come alive." It is necessary for us to mention in this matter further explanation and elaboration, so we say: when a person reflects upon the proofs indicating that Allah must be declared free of being confined to a space or direction, his skin shivers here, because establishing an existent that is neither inside the world nor outside it, neither joined to the world nor separate from it, is something difficult to conceive; here the skins shiver. But when he reflects upon the proofs indicating that He must be one, a single unity, and it is established that everything confined to a space is divisible, here his skin and heart soften to the remembrance of Allah.

Also, if he wishes his intellect to encompass the meaning of *azal* (pre-eternity), so that in his mind he advances by a thousand thousand years, then advances again by a thousand thousand years for each moment of that period, and keeps contriving and advancing and imagining in the mind, then when he strains and goes deep and thinks he has grasped the meaning of *azal*, the intellect says: "This is nothing, for everything I have grasped within me is finite, and *azal* is the existence that precedes this finite duration."
