We say: even assuming that the intended "janb" is a specific organ of Allah, exalted is He, it is impossible for neglect to occur in it, and so it is established that one must resort to interpretation (taʾwīl). The exegetes have various expressions about it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: he means, "I neglected from the reward of Allah." Muqātil said: "I neglected from the remembrance of Allah." Mujāhid said: "in the command of Allah." al-Hasan said: "in the obedience of Allah." Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "in the right of Allah." Know that multiplying these expressions does not bring relief to the breast nor cure the thirst, so we say: the "janb" is called janb because it is one of the sides of that thing, and a thing that is among the necessary attributes and consequences of a thing is as if it were one of its troops and one of its sides. When this resemblance arose between the "janb" which is the organ and that which is necessary for and follows a thing, it is for this reason that the word "janb" came to be used appropriately for truth, command and obedience. The poet said:

Do you not fear Allah regarding one who loves you (janb wāmiq), for whom a heart burns with longing for you and is torn apart?

**The third issue:** The author of *al-Kashshaf* (al-Zamakhshari) said: it is recited as *"yā ḥasratā"* (يا حسرتى) according to the original form, and as *"yā ḥasratāy"* (يا حسرتاي) with the combination of the replacement (*'iwaḍ*) and what it replaces (*mu'awwaḍ 'anhu*).

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and indeed I was among the mockers﴾. That is, he was not content with that negligence, but was among those who mocked the religion. Qatada said: "It was not enough for him to neglect the obedience of Allah until he mocked its people." The place of *"wa-in kuntu"* (وإن كنت) is an accusative of circumstance (*ḥāl*), as if he said: ﴿I neglected regarding Allah's right﴾ while I was a mocker, meaning: I neglected during my state of mockery.

The second category of the words that Allah, exalted is He, related about the people of punishment is that they mention it after the punishment has descended upon them. His saying: ﴿or say, "Had Allah guided me, I would have been among the righteous."﴾

The third category is His saying: ﴿or say when you see the punishment, "If only I had a return, so I would be among the doers of good."﴾ The summary of the speech is that this negligent one brought three things. The first: regret over neglecting obedience. The second: making the excuse of lacking guidance. The third: wishing for a return. Then Allah, exalted is He, answered their speech by saying: the excuse of lacking guidance is false, because guidance was present and the excuses were removed. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Yes! My signs had come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.﴾

Here are some issues:

**Issue one:** Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿Yes!﴾ is the answer to a negation. There is no negative word in the speech, but the meaning of negation occurs in it, because the meaning of His saying ﴿Had Allah guided me﴾ is that He did not guide me. Therefore it was fitting to mention the word *"balā"* (بلى) after it.

**Issue two:** Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The well-known recitation is in the masculine in His saying ﴿you denied them﴾, because the *nafs* (soul) can refer to the male and the female, so he was addressed in the masculine. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated from Umm Salama that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite it in the feminine. Abu 'Ubayd said: If this were established from the Prophet (ﷺ), it would be a proof that no one may leave. But it is not connected (*musnad*), because al-Rabi' did not meet Umm Salama. As for the justification for the feminine, it is that he mentioned *al-nafs*, and the word *nafs* occurs in the Qur'an mostly in the feminine, as in His saying: ﴿my soul enticed me﴾ [Ta-Ha: 96], and ﴿Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil﴾ [Yusuf: 53], and ﴿O tranquil soul﴾ [al-Fajr: 27].

**Issue three:** The Qadi said: These verses indicate the correctness of the doctrine of divine decree (*qadar*) from several aspects:

The first: It is not said, "So-and-so wronged himself," in the manner of blame, except for what comes from him. This indicates that the actions of servants occur from them, not from Allah, exalted is He.

The second: Seeking forgiveness, hoping for it, or despairing of it is only fitting if the act is the servant's act.

The third: The attribution of turning in repentance and submission to him before the punishment comes. This is only possible with his ability to attempt these two things even with the descent of the punishment, while their doctrine is that the disbeliever never has the ability to do that.

The fourth: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. This is not complete except by what is chosen for following.

The fifth: His blaming them for not perceiving what necessitates punishment, and this is not valid except with the ability to perform the act.

The sixth: Their saying: ﴿Alas, my regret over what I neglected regarding Allah﴾. A person does not regret a matter that preceded from him unless it was valid for him to do it.

The seventh: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿over what I neglected regarding Allah﴾. Whoever is not able to believe, as the people claim, and faith is not from his act, cannot be a negligent one.

[p. 8]
The eighth: His blaming them for being among the mockers. This is not complete unless mockery is their act, and it was valid for them not to do it.

The ninth: His saying: ﴿Had Allah guided me﴾, meaning: "Had He enabled me," ﴿I would have been among the righteous.﴾ Based on this, their saying: If he is not able to attain piety, how is it valid for him?

The tenth: His saying: ﴿If only I had a return, so I would be among the doers of good.﴾ According to their saying: If Allah returned him forever, return after return, and there is nothing in him except the ability of disbelief, it would not be valid for him to be a doer of good.

The eleventh: His saying, exalted is He, rebuking them: ﴿Yes! My signs had come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.﴾ So He made clear that the proof is against them for Allah, not that the proof is for them against Allah. Had the matter been as they claimed, they would have had the right to say: "The signs came to us, but You created in us the denial of them and did not enable us to affirm them."

The twelfth: He, exalted is He, described them with denial, arrogance, and disbelief, in the manner of blame. Had these things not been acts of theirs, the speech would not be valid. The answer to this is that these aspects are countered by the fact that the Qur'an is full of Allah, exalted is He, misguiding, withholding, and the emission from Him of leniency, harshness, and gradual deception (*istidraj*). Since this exegesis is full of that, there is no need for repetition.

ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ

ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ

*(Qur'an 39:60–61)*

اعْلَمْ أنَّ هَذا مِن نَوْعٍ آخَرَ مِن تَقْرِيرِ الوَعِيدِ والوَعْدِ، أمّا الوَعِيدُ فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وفِيهِ بَحْثانِ، أحَدُهُما: أنَّ هَذا التَّكْذِيبَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟ والثّانِي: أنَّ هَذا السَّوادَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟

Know that this is from another type of affirmation of the threat (wa'id) and the promise (wa'd). As for the threat, it is the words of the Exalted: "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened." In this there are two investigations: first, what is the nature of this lying? Second, what is the nature of this blackness?

البَحْثُ الأوَّلُ: عَنْ حَقِيقَةِ هَذا التَّكْذِيبِ، فَنَقُولُ: المَشْهُورُ أنَّ الكَذِبَ هو الإخْبارُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ عَلى خِلافِ ما هو عَلَيْهِ، ومِنهم مَن قالَ: هَذا القَدْرُ لا يَكُونُ كَذِبًا بَلِ الشَّرْطُ في كَوْنِهِ كَذِبًا أنْ يَقْصِدَ الإتْيانَ بِخَبَرٍ يُخالِفُ المُخْبَرَ عَنْهُ، إذا عَرَفْتَ هَذا الأصْلَ فَنَذْكُرُ أقْوالَ النّاسِ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ:

The first investigation concerns the reality of this lying. We say: the well-known view is that lying is informing about a thing contrary to what it actually is. Others said: this degree alone is not lying; rather, the condition for it being lying is that the speaker intends to convey a report that contradicts what he reports about. Once you know this principle, we shall mention the opinions of people concerning this verse:

قالَ الكَعْبِيُّ: ويَرُدُّ الجَبْرَ بِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ورَدَتْ عَقِيبَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ يَعْنِي أنَّهُ ما هَدانِي بَلْ أضَلَّنِي، فَلَمّا حَكى اللَّهُ عَنِ الكُفّارِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ عَقِيبَهُ ﴿تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ هَذا عائِدًا إلى ذَلِكَ الكَلامِ المُتَقَدِّمِ، ثُمَّ رُوِيَ عَنِ الحَسَنِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ قالَ: ”«ما بالُ أقْوامٍ يُصَلُّونَ ويَقْرَءُونَ القُرْآنَ، يَزْعُمُونَ أنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الذُّنُوبَ عَلى العِبادِ، وهم كَذَبَةٌ عَلى اللَّهِ، واللَّهُ مُسَوِّدٌ وُجُوهَهم»“ . واعْلَمْ أنَّ أصْحابَنا قالُوا: آخِرُ الآيَةِ يَدُلُّ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا التَّأْوِيلِ؛ لِأنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ في آخِرِ الآيَةِ: ﴿ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ وهَذا يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صارَتْ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةً أقْوامٌ مُتَكَبِّرُونَ، والتَّكَبُّرُ لا يَلِيقُ بِمَن يَقُولُ: أنا لا أقْدِرُ عَلى الخَلْقِ والإعادَةِ والإيجادِ، وإنَّما القادِرُ عَلَيْهِ هو اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى، أمّا الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ يُرِيدُ شَيْئًا وأنا أُرِيدُ بِضِدِّهِ، فَيَحْصُلُ مُرادِي ولا يَحْصُلُ مُرادُ اللَّهِ، فالتَّكَبُّرُ بِهَذا القائِلِ ألْيَقُ، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ هَذا التَّأْوِيلَ الَّذِي ذَكَرُوهُ فاسِدٌ، ومِنَ النّاسِ مَن قالَ: إنَّ هَذا الوَعِيدَ مُخْتَصٌّ بِاليَهُودِ والنَّصارى، ومِنهم مَن قالَ:

Al-Ka'bi said: he refutes compulsion (jabr) by saying that this verse came immediately after the statement, "If only God had guided me," meaning that He did not guide him but misguided him. When God related the words of the disbelievers and then, right after them, mentioned, "You will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," it must be that this refers back to that preceding speech. Then it is narrated from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "What is wrong with people who pray and recite the Qur'an, claiming that God has decreed sins upon His servants, while they are liars against God, and God blackens their faces." Know that our companions said: the end of the verse indicates the corruption of this interpretation, because He, Exalted, said at the end of the verse: "Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?" This indicates that those whose faces became blackened are arrogant people, and arrogance does not befit one who says, "I am not able to create, to bring back, or to originate," since the One who is able to do this is God, glory be to Him. As for those who say, "God wills something, and I will the opposite, so my will is accomplished and God's will is not," arrogance is more fitting for this speaker. Thus it is established that the interpretation they mentioned is corrupt. Among people there are those who said that this threat is specific to the Jews and Christians, and among them are those who said:

صفحة ٩

إنَّهُ مُخْتَصٌّ بِمُشْرِكِي العَرَبِ، قالَ القاضِي: يَجِبُ حَمْلُ الآيَةِ عَلى الكُلِّ مِنَ المُشَبِّهَةِ والمُجْبِرَةِ، وكَذَلِكَ كُلُّ مَن وصَفَ اللَّهَ بِما لا يَلِيقُ بِهِ نَفْيًا وإثْباتًا، فَأضافَ إلَيْهِ ما يَجِبُ تَنْزِيهُهُ عَنْهُ أوْ نَزَّهَهُ عَمّا يَجِبُ أنْ يُضافَ إلَيْهِ، فالكُلُّ مِنهم داخِلُونَ تَحْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ؛ لِأنَّهم كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ، فَتَخْصِيصُ الآيَةِ بِالمُجْبِرَةِ والمُشَبِّهَةِ أوِ اليَهُودِ والنَّصارى لا يَجُوزُ، واعْلَمْ أنّا لَوْ أجْرَيْنا هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَلى عُمُومِها كَما ذَكَرَهُ القاضِي لَزِمَهُ تَكْفِيرُ الأُمَّةِ؛ لِأنَّكَ لا تَرى فِرْقَةً مِن فِرَقِ الأُمَّةِ إلّا وقَدْ حَصَلَ بَيْنَهُمُ اخْتِلافٌ شَدِيدٌ في صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ حَصَلَ الِاخْتِلافُ بَيْنَ أبِي هاشِمٍ وأهْلِ السُّنَّةِ في مَسائِلَ كَثِيرَةٍ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ويَلْزَمُ عَلى قانُونِ قَوْلِ القاضِي تَكْفِيرُ أحَدِهِما، فَثَبَتَ أنَّهُ يَجِبُ أنْ يُحْمَلَ الكَذِبُ المَذْكُورُ في الآيَةِ عَلى ما إذا قَصَدَ الإخْبارَ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ أنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أنَّهُ كاذِبٌ فِيما يَقُولُ، ومِثالُ هَذا كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ فَإنَّهم كانُوا يَصِفُونَ تِلْكَ الأصْنامَ بِالإلَهِيَّةِ مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ بِالضَّرُورَةِ أنَّها جَماداتٌ، وكانُوا يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى حَرَّمَ البَحِيرَةَ والسّائِبَةَ والوَصِيلَةَ والحامَ، مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يُنْكِرُونَ القَوْلَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ كَذا وأباحَ كَذا، وكانَ قائِلُهُ عالِمًا بِأنَّهُ كَذِبٌ، وإذا كانَ كَذَلِكَ فَإلْحاقُ مِثْلَ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهَذا الجاهِلِ الكَذّابِ الضّالِّ المُضِلِّ يَكُونُ مُناسِبًا، أمّا مَن لَمْ يَقْصِدْ إلّا الحَقَّ والصِّدْقَ لَكِنَّهُ أخْطَأ، يَبْعُدُ إلْحاقُ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهِ.

that it is specific to the idolaters of the Arabs. The judge (al-Qadi) said: the verse must be applied to all of the Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) and the Mujbira (determinists), and likewise every person who describes God, by negation or affirmation, in a manner unbefitting Him, attributing to Him what must be declared far from Him, or declaring Him far from what must be attributed to Him. All of them are included under this verse, because they lied against God. Therefore restricting the verse to the Mujbira and Mushabbiha, or to the Jews and Christians, is not permissible. Know that if we applied this verse to its generality, as the judge stated, it would entail declaring the entire community (ummah) to be disbelievers, because you will not find any sect of the community without a severe disagreement concerning the attributes of God, exalted is He. Do you not see that disagreement arose between Abu Hashim and the People of the Sunnah on many issues concerning God's attributes? According to the principle of the judge's view, one of them would have to be declared a disbeliever. Thus it is established that the lying mentioned in the verse must be understood as the case where one intends to report about a thing while knowing that he is lying in what he says. An example of this is the disbelievers of Quraysh, for they described those idols as divine while knowingly recognizing by necessity that they were inanimate objects, and they used to say that God had forbidden the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and the ham, while they denied the claim that God had forbidden such-and-such or permitted such-and-such, and the one who said it knew it was a lie. If that is so, then attaching this kind of threat to this ignorant, lying, misguided, and misleading person is appropriate. As for one who intended nothing but truth and sincerity but erred, it is far-fetched to attach this threat to him.

البَحْثُ الثّانِي: الكَلامُ في كَيْفِيَّةِ السَّوادِ الحاصِلِ في وُجُوهِهِمْ، والأقْرَبُ أنَّهُ سَوادٌ مُخالِفٌ لِسائِرِ أنْواعِ السَّوادِ، وهو سَوادٌ يَدُلُّ عَلى الجَهْلِ بِاللَّهِ والكَذِبِ عَلى اللَّهِ، وأقُولُ: إنَّ الجَهْلَ ظُلْمَةٌ، والظُّلْمَةُ تُتَخَيَّلُ كَأنَّها سَوادٌ، فَسَوادُ قُلُوبِهِمْ أوْجَبَ سَوادَ وُجُوهِهِمْ، وتَحْتَ هَذا الكَلامِ أسْرارٌ عَمِيقَةٌ مِن مَباحِثِ أحْوالِ القِيامَةِ، فَلَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ هَذا الوَعِيدَ أرْدَفَهُ بِالوَعْدِ فَقالَ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ الآيَةَ، قالَ القاضِي: المُرادُ بِهِ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ؛ إذْ لا يُوصَفُ بِالِاتِّقاءِ المُطْلَقِ إلّا مَن كانَ هَذا حالَهُ، فَيُقالُ لَهُ: أمْرُكَ عَجِيبٌ جِدًّا فَإنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يُحْمَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ عَلى الَّذِينَ قالُوا: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ فَعَلى هَذا القانُونِ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى بَعْدَهُ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ هُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ذَلِكَ الكَذِبَ، فَهَذا يَقْتَضِي أنَّ كُلَّ مَن لَمْ يَتَّصِفْ بِذَلِكَ الكَذِبِ أنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ تَحْتَ ذَلِكَ الوَعْدِ المَذْكُورِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وأنْ يَكُونَ قَوْلُكَ: ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ المُرادُ مِنهُ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ فاسِدًا، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ التَّعَصُّبَ يَحْمِلُ الرَّجُلَ العاقِلَ عَلى الكَلِماتِ المُتَناقِضَةِ، بَلِ الحَقُّ أنْ تَقُولَ: المُتَّقِي هو الآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ، والآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ في صُورَةٍ واحِدَةٍ آتٍ بِمُسَمّى الِاتِّقاءِ، وبِهَذا الحَرْفِ قُلْنا: الأمْرُ المُطْلَقُ لا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرارَ، ثُمَّ ذَلِكَ الِاتِّقاءُ غَيْرُ مَذْكُورٍ بِعَيْنِهِ في هَذِهِ اللَّفْظَةِ فَوَجَبَ حَمْلُهُ عَلى الِاتِّقاءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ الَّذِي سَبَقَ ذِكْرَهُ، وهَذا هو الكَذِبُ عَلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ ظاهِرَ الآيَةِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ مَنِ اتَّقى عَنْ تِلْكَ الصِّفَةِ وجَبَ دُخُولُهُ تَحْتَ هَذا الوَعْدِ الكَرِيمِ.

The second investigation concerns the manner of the blackness that appears on their faces. The closest view is that it is a blackness different from all other kinds of blackness, one that indicates ignorance of God and lying against God. I say: ignorance is darkness, and darkness is imagined as if it were blackness; so the blackness of their hearts necessitated the blackness of their faces. Beneath this discussion lie profound secrets from the investigations into the conditions of the Resurrection. When God mentioned this threat, He followed it with a promise, saying: "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and so on. The judge said: what is meant by it is the one who was mindful of all the major sins, since "mindfulness" in an absolute sense is not ascribed except to one whose state is this. It is said to him: your position is extremely strange, for you said, when the words of the Exalted were mentioned, "If only God had guided me, I would have been among the mindful," it is necessary that His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," be understood as referring to those who said, "If only God had guided me." By this principle, when His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," preceded, and then He, Exalted, said after it, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," it must be that the intended ones are those who were mindful of that lying. This implies that everyone who was not characterized by that lying is included under that promise mentioned in His words, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and that your saying, "those who were mindful," meaning those who were mindful of all the major sins, is corrupt. Thus it is established that partisanship drives an intelligent man to contradictory statements. Rather, the truth is that you should say: the mindful one is the one who performs mindfulness, and the one who performs mindfulness in a single instance has performed the designation of mindfulness. And by this very letter we said: an absolute command does not indicate repetition. Then that mindfulness is not specified by name in this expression, so it must be understood as mindfulness regarding the thing previously mentioned, and this is lying against God, the Exalted. Thus it is established that the apparent meaning of the verse requires that whoever was mindful regarding that attribute must be included under this noble promise.

* * *

Then He, Exalted, said: "bi-mafazatihim" (with their place of salvation). Concerning this there are several issues:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قَرَأ حَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ ”بِمَفازاتِهِمْ“ عَلى الجَمْعِ، والباقُونَ بِمَفازَتِهِمْ عَلى التَّوْحِيدِ، وحَكى الواحِدِيُّ عَنِ الفَرّاءِ أنَّهُ قالَ: كِلاهُما صَوابٌ؛ إذْ يُقالُ في الكَلامِ: قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ أمْرُ القَوْمِ،

صفحة ١٠

وأُمُورُ القَوْمِ، قالَ أبُو عَلِيٍّ الفارِسِيُّ: الإفْرادُ لِلْمَصْدَرِ ووَجْهُ الجَمْعِ أنَّ المَصادِرَ قَدْ تُجْمَعُ إذا اخْتَلَفَتْ أجْناسُها، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَ﴾ [الأحْزابِ: ١٠] ولا شَكَّ أنَّ لِكُلِّ مُتَّقٍ نَوْعًا آخَرَ مِنَ المَفازَةِ.

First issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read "bi-mafazatihim" in the plural (*mafazatihim*), while the rest read *bi-mafazatihim* in the singular. Al-Wahidi related from al-Farra' that he said: both are correct, since it is said in speech: "the matter of the people has become clear," and "the affairs of the people." Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the singular is the verbal noun (masdar), and the reason for the plural is that verbal nouns may be pluralized when their kinds differ, as in the words of the Exalted: "and you assume about God assumptions" (al-Ahzab 33:10). There is no doubt that each one who is mindful has a different kind of salvation.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: المَفازَةُ مَفْعَلَةٌ مِنَ الفَوْزِ وهو السَّعادَةُ، فَكَأنَّ المَعْنى أنَّ النَّجاةَ في القِيامَةِ حَصَلَتْ بِسَبَبِ فَوْزِهِمْ في الدُّنْيا بِالطّاعاتِ والخَيْراتِ، فَعَبَّرَ عَنِ الفَوْزِ بِأوْقاتِها ومَواضِعِها.

Second issue: *al-mafazah* is of the form *mafalah* (a noun of place or time, *maf'alah*) derived from *al-fawz*, which is success or felicity. So the meaning seems to be that the deliverance on the Day of Resurrection was achieved through their success in this world by means of acts of obedience and good deeds; thus He expressed the success by its times and places.

* * *

ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ والمُرادُ أنَّهُ كالتَّفْسِيرِ لِتِلْكَ النَّجاةِ، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ يُنَجِّيهِمْ؟ فَقِيلَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ وهَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ جامِعَةٌ؛ لِأنَّهُ إذا عَلِمَ أنَّهُ لا يَمَسُّهُ السُّوءُ كانَ فارِغَ البالِ بِحَسْبِ الحالِ عَمّا وقَعَ في قَلْبِهِ بِسَبَبِ فَواتِ الماضِي، فَحِينَئِذٍ يَظْهَرُ أنَّهُ سَلِمَ عَنْ كُلِّ الآفاتِ، ونَسْألُ اللَّهَ الفَوْزَ بِهَذِهِ الدَّرَجاتِ بِمَنِّهِ وكَرَمِهِ.

Then He said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning is that this is like an explanation of that deliverance, as if it were said: how will He deliver them? So it was said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." This is a comprehensive expression, because when one knows that evil will not touch him, he is at ease in his state regarding what had occurred in his heart through the loss of the past. Then it becomes evident that he is safe from every calamity. We ask God for success in attaining these ranks by His bounty and generosity.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ لا يَنالُهُمُ الخَوْفُ والرُّعْبُ في القِيامَةِ، وتَأكَّدَ هَذا بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ .

Third issue: the verse indicates that the believers will not be touched by fear or terror on the Day of Resurrection, and this is confirmed by His words: "The greatest terror will not grieve them" (al-Anbiya' 21:103).

ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ

ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ

*(Qur'an 39:60–61)*

اعْلَمْ أنَّ هَذا مِن نَوْعٍ آخَرَ مِن تَقْرِيرِ الوَعِيدِ والوَعْدِ، أمّا الوَعِيدُ فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وفِيهِ بَحْثانِ، أحَدُهُما: أنَّ هَذا التَّكْذِيبَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟ والثّانِي: أنَّ هَذا السَّوادَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟

Know that this is from another type of affirmation of the threat (wa'id) and the promise (wa'd). As for the threat, it is the words of the Exalted: "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened." In this there are two investigations: first, what is the nature of this lying? Second, what is the nature of this blackness?

البَحْثُ الأوَّلُ: عَنْ حَقِيقَةِ هَذا التَّكْذِيبِ، فَنَقُولُ: المَشْهُورُ أنَّ الكَذِبَ هو الإخْبارُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ عَلى خِلافِ ما هو عَلَيْهِ، ومِنهم مَن قالَ: هَذا القَدْرُ لا يَكُونُ كَذِبًا بَلِ الشَّرْطُ في كَوْنِهِ كَذِبًا أنْ يَقْصِدَ الإتْيانَ بِخَبَرٍ يُخالِفُ المُخْبَرَ عَنْهُ، إذا عَرَفْتَ هَذا الأصْلَ فَنَذْكُرُ أقْوالَ النّاسِ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ:

The first investigation concerns the reality of this lying. We say: the well-known view is that lying is informing about a thing contrary to what it actually is. Others said: this degree alone is not lying; rather, the condition for it being lying is that the speaker intends to convey a report that contradicts what he reports about. Once you know this principle, we shall mention the opinions of people concerning this verse:

قالَ الكَعْبِيُّ: ويَرُدُّ الجَبْرَ بِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ورَدَتْ عَقِيبَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ يَعْنِي أنَّهُ ما هَدانِي بَلْ أضَلَّنِي، فَلَمّا حَكى اللَّهُ عَنِ الكُفّارِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ عَقِيبَهُ ﴿تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ هَذا عائِدًا إلى ذَلِكَ الكَلامِ المُتَقَدِّمِ، ثُمَّ رُوِيَ عَنِ الحَسَنِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ قالَ: ”«ما بالُ أقْوامٍ يُصَلُّونَ ويَقْرَءُونَ القُرْآنَ، يَزْعُمُونَ أنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الذُّنُوبَ عَلى العِبادِ، وهم كَذَبَةٌ عَلى اللَّهِ، واللَّهُ مُسَوِّدٌ وُجُوهَهم»“ . واعْلَمْ أنَّ أصْحابَنا قالُوا: آخِرُ الآيَةِ يَدُلُّ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا التَّأْوِيلِ؛ لِأنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ في آخِرِ الآيَةِ: ﴿ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ وهَذا يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صارَتْ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةً أقْوامٌ مُتَكَبِّرُونَ، والتَّكَبُّرُ لا يَلِيقُ بِمَن يَقُولُ: أنا لا أقْدِرُ عَلى الخَلْقِ والإعادَةِ والإيجادِ، وإنَّما القادِرُ عَلَيْهِ هو اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى، أمّا الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ يُرِيدُ شَيْئًا وأنا أُرِيدُ بِضِدِّهِ، فَيَحْصُلُ مُرادِي ولا يَحْصُلُ مُرادُ اللَّهِ، فالتَّكَبُّرُ بِهَذا القائِلِ ألْيَقُ، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ هَذا التَّأْوِيلَ الَّذِي ذَكَرُوهُ فاسِدٌ، ومِنَ النّاسِ مَن قالَ: إنَّ هَذا الوَعِيدَ مُخْتَصٌّ بِاليَهُودِ والنَّصارى، ومِنهم مَن قالَ:

Al-Ka'bi said: he refutes compulsion (jabr) by saying that this verse came immediately after the statement, "If only God had guided me," meaning that He did not guide him but misguided him. When God related the words of the disbelievers and then, right after them, mentioned, "You will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," it must be that this refers back to that preceding speech. Then it is narrated from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "What is wrong with people who pray and recite the Qur'an, claiming that God has decreed sins upon His servants, while they are liars against God, and God blackens their faces." Know that our companions said: the end of the verse indicates the corruption of this interpretation, because He, Exalted, said at the end of the verse: "Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?" This indicates that those whose faces became blackened are arrogant people, and arrogance does not befit one who says, "I am not able to create, to bring back, or to originate," since the One who is able to do this is God, glory be to Him. As for those who say, "God wills something, and I will the opposite, so my will is accomplished and God's will is not," arrogance is more fitting for this speaker. Thus it is established that the interpretation they mentioned is corrupt. Among people there are those who said that this threat is specific to the Jews and Christians, and among them are those who said:

صفحة ٩

إنَّهُ مُخْتَصٌّ بِمُشْرِكِي العَرَبِ، قالَ القاضِي: يَجِبُ حَمْلُ الآيَةِ عَلى الكُلِّ مِنَ المُشَبِّهَةِ والمُجْبِرَةِ، وكَذَلِكَ كُلُّ مَن وصَفَ اللَّهَ بِما لا يَلِيقُ بِهِ نَفْيًا وإثْباتًا، فَأضافَ إلَيْهِ ما يَجِبُ تَنْزِيهُهُ عَنْهُ أوْ نَزَّهَهُ عَمّا يَجِبُ أنْ يُضافَ إلَيْهِ، فالكُلُّ مِنهم داخِلُونَ تَحْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ؛ لِأنَّهم كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ، فَتَخْصِيصُ الآيَةِ بِالمُجْبِرَةِ والمُشَبِّهَةِ أوِ اليَهُودِ والنَّصارى لا يَجُوزُ، واعْلَمْ أنّا لَوْ أجْرَيْنا هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَلى عُمُومِها كَما ذَكَرَهُ القاضِي لَزِمَهُ تَكْفِيرُ الأُمَّةِ؛ لِأنَّكَ لا تَرى فِرْقَةً مِن فِرَقِ الأُمَّةِ إلّا وقَدْ حَصَلَ بَيْنَهُمُ اخْتِلافٌ شَدِيدٌ في صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ حَصَلَ الِاخْتِلافُ بَيْنَ أبِي هاشِمٍ وأهْلِ السُّنَّةِ في مَسائِلَ كَثِيرَةٍ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ويَلْزَمُ عَلى قانُونِ قَوْلِ القاضِي تَكْفِيرُ أحَدِهِما، فَثَبَتَ أنَّهُ يَجِبُ أنْ يُحْمَلَ الكَذِبُ المَذْكُورُ في الآيَةِ عَلى ما إذا قَصَدَ الإخْبارَ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ أنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أنَّهُ كاذِبٌ فِيما يَقُولُ، ومِثالُ هَذا كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ فَإنَّهم كانُوا يَصِفُونَ تِلْكَ الأصْنامَ بِالإلَهِيَّةِ مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ بِالضَّرُورَةِ أنَّها جَماداتٌ، وكانُوا يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى حَرَّمَ البَحِيرَةَ والسّائِبَةَ والوَصِيلَةَ والحامَ، مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يُنْكِرُونَ القَوْلَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ كَذا وأباحَ كَذا، وكانَ قائِلُهُ عالِمًا بِأنَّهُ كَذِبٌ، وإذا كانَ كَذَلِكَ فَإلْحاقُ مِثْلَ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهَذا الجاهِلِ الكَذّابِ الضّالِّ المُضِلِّ يَكُونُ مُناسِبًا، أمّا مَن لَمْ يَقْصِدْ إلّا الحَقَّ والصِّدْقَ لَكِنَّهُ أخْطَأ، يَبْعُدُ إلْحاقُ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهِ.

that it is specific to the idolaters of the Arabs. The judge (al-Qadi) said: the verse must be applied to all of the Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) and the Mujbira (determinists), and likewise every person who describes God, by negation or affirmation, in a manner unbefitting Him, attributing to Him what must be declared far from Him, or declaring Him far from what must be attributed to Him. All of them are included under this verse, because they lied against God. Therefore restricting the verse to the Mujbira and Mushabbiha, or to the Jews and Christians, is not permissible. Know that if we applied this verse to its generality, as the judge stated, it would entail declaring the entire community (ummah) to be disbelievers, because you will not find any sect of the community without a severe disagreement concerning the attributes of God, exalted is He. Do you not see that disagreement arose between Abu Hashim and the People of the Sunnah on many issues concerning God's attributes? According to the principle of the judge's view, one of them would have to be declared a disbeliever. Thus it is established that the lying mentioned in the verse must be understood as the case where one intends to report about a thing while knowing that he is lying in what he says. An example of this is the disbelievers of Quraysh, for they described those idols as divine while knowingly recognizing by necessity that they were inanimate objects, and they used to say that God had forbidden the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and the ham, while they denied the claim that God had forbidden such-and-such or permitted such-and-such, and the one who said it knew it was a lie. If that is so, then attaching this kind of threat to this ignorant, lying, misguided, and misleading person is appropriate. As for one who intended nothing but truth and sincerity but erred, it is far-fetched to attach this threat to him.

البَحْثُ الثّانِي: الكَلامُ في كَيْفِيَّةِ السَّوادِ الحاصِلِ في وُجُوهِهِمْ، والأقْرَبُ أنَّهُ سَوادٌ مُخالِفٌ لِسائِرِ أنْواعِ السَّوادِ، وهو سَوادٌ يَدُلُّ عَلى الجَهْلِ بِاللَّهِ والكَذِبِ عَلى اللَّهِ، وأقُولُ: إنَّ الجَهْلَ ظُلْمَةٌ، والظُّلْمَةُ تُتَخَيَّلُ كَأنَّها سَوادٌ، فَسَوادُ قُلُوبِهِمْ أوْجَبَ سَوادَ وُجُوهِهِمْ، وتَحْتَ هَذا الكَلامِ أسْرارٌ عَمِيقَةٌ مِن مَباحِثِ أحْوالِ القِيامَةِ، فَلَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ هَذا الوَعِيدَ أرْدَفَهُ بِالوَعْدِ فَقالَ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ الآيَةَ، قالَ القاضِي: المُرادُ بِهِ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ؛ إذْ لا يُوصَفُ بِالِاتِّقاءِ المُطْلَقِ إلّا مَن كانَ هَذا حالَهُ، فَيُقالُ لَهُ: أمْرُكَ عَجِيبٌ جِدًّا فَإنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يُحْمَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ عَلى الَّذِينَ قالُوا: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ فَعَلى هَذا القانُونِ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى بَعْدَهُ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ هُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ذَلِكَ الكَذِبَ، فَهَذا يَقْتَضِي أنَّ كُلَّ مَن لَمْ يَتَّصِفْ بِذَلِكَ الكَذِبِ أنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ تَحْتَ ذَلِكَ الوَعْدِ المَذْكُورِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وأنْ يَكُونَ قَوْلُكَ: ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ المُرادُ مِنهُ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ فاسِدًا، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ التَّعَصُّبَ يَحْمِلُ الرَّجُلَ العاقِلَ عَلى الكَلِماتِ المُتَناقِضَةِ، بَلِ الحَقُّ أنْ تَقُولَ: المُتَّقِي هو الآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ، والآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ في صُورَةٍ واحِدَةٍ آتٍ بِمُسَمّى الِاتِّقاءِ، وبِهَذا الحَرْفِ قُلْنا: الأمْرُ المُطْلَقُ لا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرارَ، ثُمَّ ذَلِكَ الِاتِّقاءُ غَيْرُ مَذْكُورٍ بِعَيْنِهِ في هَذِهِ اللَّفْظَةِ فَوَجَبَ حَمْلُهُ عَلى الِاتِّقاءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ الَّذِي سَبَقَ ذِكْرَهُ، وهَذا هو الكَذِبُ عَلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ ظاهِرَ الآيَةِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ مَنِ اتَّقى عَنْ تِلْكَ الصِّفَةِ وجَبَ دُخُولُهُ تَحْتَ هَذا الوَعْدِ الكَرِيمِ.

The second investigation concerns the manner of the blackness that appears on their faces. The closest view is that it is a blackness different from all other kinds of blackness, one that indicates ignorance of God and lying against God. I say: ignorance is darkness, and darkness is imagined as if it were blackness; so the blackness of their hearts necessitated the blackness of their faces. Beneath this discussion lie profound secrets from the investigations into the conditions of the Resurrection. When God mentioned this threat, He followed it with a promise, saying: "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and so on. The judge said: what is meant by it is the one who was mindful of all the major sins, since "mindfulness" in an absolute sense is not ascribed except to one whose state is this. It is said to him: your position is extremely strange, for you said, when the words of the Exalted were mentioned, "If only God had guided me, I would have been among the mindful," it is necessary that His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," be understood as referring to those who said, "If only God had guided me." By this principle, when His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," preceded, and then He, Exalted, said after it, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," it must be that the intended ones are those who were mindful of that lying. This implies that everyone who was not characterized by that lying is included under that promise mentioned in His words, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and that your saying, "those who were mindful," meaning those who were mindful of all the major sins, is corrupt. Thus it is established that partisanship drives an intelligent man to contradictory statements. Rather, the truth is that you should say: the mindful one is the one who performs mindfulness, and the one who performs mindfulness in a single instance has performed the designation of mindfulness. And by this very letter we said: an absolute command does not indicate repetition. Then that mindfulness is not specified by name in this expression, so it must be understood as mindfulness regarding the thing previously mentioned, and this is lying against God, the Exalted. Thus it is established that the apparent meaning of the verse requires that whoever was mindful regarding that attribute must be included under this noble promise.

* * *

Then He, Exalted, said: "bi-mafazatihim" (with their place of salvation). Concerning this there are several issues:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قَرَأ حَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ ”بِمَفازاتِهِمْ“ عَلى الجَمْعِ، والباقُونَ بِمَفازَتِهِمْ عَلى التَّوْحِيدِ، وحَكى الواحِدِيُّ عَنِ الفَرّاءِ أنَّهُ قالَ: كِلاهُما صَوابٌ؛ إذْ يُقالُ في الكَلامِ: قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ أمْرُ القَوْمِ،

صفحة ١٠

وأُمُورُ القَوْمِ، قالَ أبُو عَلِيٍّ الفارِسِيُّ: الإفْرادُ لِلْمَصْدَرِ ووَجْهُ الجَمْعِ أنَّ المَصادِرَ قَدْ تُجْمَعُ إذا اخْتَلَفَتْ أجْناسُها، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَ﴾ [الأحْزابِ: ١٠] ولا شَكَّ أنَّ لِكُلِّ مُتَّقٍ نَوْعًا آخَرَ مِنَ المَفازَةِ.

First issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read "bi-mafazatihim" in the plural (*mafazatihim*), while the rest read *bi-mafazatihim* in the singular. Al-Wahidi related from al-Farra' that he said: both are correct, since it is said in speech: "the matter of the people has become clear," and "the affairs of the people." Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the singular is the verbal noun (masdar), and the reason for the plural is that verbal nouns may be pluralized when their kinds differ, as in the words of the Exalted: "and you assume about God assumptions" (al-Ahzab 33:10). There is no doubt that each one who is mindful has a different kind of salvation.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: المَفازَةُ مَفْعَلَةٌ مِنَ الفَوْزِ وهو السَّعادَةُ، فَكَأنَّ المَعْنى أنَّ النَّجاةَ في القِيامَةِ حَصَلَتْ بِسَبَبِ فَوْزِهِمْ في الدُّنْيا بِالطّاعاتِ والخَيْراتِ، فَعَبَّرَ عَنِ الفَوْزِ بِأوْقاتِها ومَواضِعِها.

Second issue: *al-mafazah* is of the form *mafalah* (a noun of place or time, *maf'alah*) derived from *al-fawz*, which is success or felicity. So the meaning seems to be that the deliverance on the Day of Resurrection was achieved through their success in this world by means of acts of obedience and good deeds; thus He expressed the success by its times and places.

* * *

ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ والمُرادُ أنَّهُ كالتَّفْسِيرِ لِتِلْكَ النَّجاةِ، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ يُنَجِّيهِمْ؟ فَقِيلَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ وهَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ جامِعَةٌ؛ لِأنَّهُ إذا عَلِمَ أنَّهُ لا يَمَسُّهُ السُّوءُ كانَ فارِغَ البالِ بِحَسْبِ الحالِ عَمّا وقَعَ في قَلْبِهِ بِسَبَبِ فَواتِ الماضِي، فَحِينَئِذٍ يَظْهَرُ أنَّهُ سَلِمَ عَنْ كُلِّ الآفاتِ، ونَسْألُ اللَّهَ الفَوْزَ بِهَذِهِ الدَّرَجاتِ بِمَنِّهِ وكَرَمِهِ.

Then He said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning is that this is like an explanation of that deliverance, as if it were said: how will He deliver them? So it was said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." This is a comprehensive expression, because when one knows that evil will not touch him, he is at ease in his state regarding what had occurred in his heart through the loss of the past. Then it becomes evident that he is safe from every calamity. We ask God for success in attaining these ranks by His bounty and generosity.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ لا يَنالُهُمُ الخَوْفُ والرُّعْبُ في القِيامَةِ، وتَأكَّدَ هَذا بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ .

Third issue: the verse indicates that the believers will not be touched by fear or terror on the Day of Resurrection, and this is confirmed by His words: "The greatest terror will not grieve them" (al-Anbiya' 21:103).

ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ

ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ

*(Qur'an 39:60–61)*

اعْلَمْ أنَّ هَذا مِن نَوْعٍ آخَرَ مِن تَقْرِيرِ الوَعِيدِ والوَعْدِ، أمّا الوَعِيدُ فَقَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وفِيهِ بَحْثانِ، أحَدُهُما: أنَّ هَذا التَّكْذِيبَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟ والثّانِي: أنَّ هَذا السَّوادَ كَيْفَ هُوَ؟

Know that this is from another type of affirmation of the threat (wa'id) and the promise (wa'd). As for the threat, it is the words of the Exalted: "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened." In this there are two investigations: first, what is the nature of this lying? Second, what is the nature of this blackness?

البَحْثُ الأوَّلُ: عَنْ حَقِيقَةِ هَذا التَّكْذِيبِ، فَنَقُولُ: المَشْهُورُ أنَّ الكَذِبَ هو الإخْبارُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ عَلى خِلافِ ما هو عَلَيْهِ، ومِنهم مَن قالَ: هَذا القَدْرُ لا يَكُونُ كَذِبًا بَلِ الشَّرْطُ في كَوْنِهِ كَذِبًا أنْ يَقْصِدَ الإتْيانَ بِخَبَرٍ يُخالِفُ المُخْبَرَ عَنْهُ، إذا عَرَفْتَ هَذا الأصْلَ فَنَذْكُرُ أقْوالَ النّاسِ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ:

The first investigation concerns the reality of this lying. We say: the well-known view is that lying is informing about a thing contrary to what it actually is. Others said: this degree alone is not lying; rather, the condition for it being lying is that the speaker intends to convey a report that contradicts what he reports about. Once you know this principle, we shall mention the opinions of people concerning this verse:

قالَ الكَعْبِيُّ: ويَرُدُّ الجَبْرَ بِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ورَدَتْ عَقِيبَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ يَعْنِي أنَّهُ ما هَدانِي بَلْ أضَلَّنِي، فَلَمّا حَكى اللَّهُ عَنِ الكُفّارِ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ عَقِيبَهُ ﴿تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ هَذا عائِدًا إلى ذَلِكَ الكَلامِ المُتَقَدِّمِ، ثُمَّ رُوِيَ عَنِ الحَسَنِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أنَّهُ قالَ: ”«ما بالُ أقْوامٍ يُصَلُّونَ ويَقْرَءُونَ القُرْآنَ، يَزْعُمُونَ أنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ الذُّنُوبَ عَلى العِبادِ، وهم كَذَبَةٌ عَلى اللَّهِ، واللَّهُ مُسَوِّدٌ وُجُوهَهم»“ . واعْلَمْ أنَّ أصْحابَنا قالُوا: آخِرُ الآيَةِ يَدُلُّ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا التَّأْوِيلِ؛ لِأنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ في آخِرِ الآيَةِ: ﴿ألَيْسَ في جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ وهَذا يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صارَتْ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةً أقْوامٌ مُتَكَبِّرُونَ، والتَّكَبُّرُ لا يَلِيقُ بِمَن يَقُولُ: أنا لا أقْدِرُ عَلى الخَلْقِ والإعادَةِ والإيجادِ، وإنَّما القادِرُ عَلَيْهِ هو اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى، أمّا الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ يُرِيدُ شَيْئًا وأنا أُرِيدُ بِضِدِّهِ، فَيَحْصُلُ مُرادِي ولا يَحْصُلُ مُرادُ اللَّهِ، فالتَّكَبُّرُ بِهَذا القائِلِ ألْيَقُ، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ هَذا التَّأْوِيلَ الَّذِي ذَكَرُوهُ فاسِدٌ، ومِنَ النّاسِ مَن قالَ: إنَّ هَذا الوَعِيدَ مُخْتَصٌّ بِاليَهُودِ والنَّصارى، ومِنهم مَن قالَ:

Al-Ka'bi said: he refutes compulsion (jabr) by saying that this verse came immediately after the statement, "If only God had guided me," meaning that He did not guide him but misguided him. When God related the words of the disbelievers and then, right after them, mentioned, "You will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," it must be that this refers back to that preceding speech. Then it is narrated from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "What is wrong with people who pray and recite the Qur'an, claiming that God has decreed sins upon His servants, while they are liars against God, and God blackens their faces." Know that our companions said: the end of the verse indicates the corruption of this interpretation, because He, Exalted, said at the end of the verse: "Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?" This indicates that those whose faces became blackened are arrogant people, and arrogance does not befit one who says, "I am not able to create, to bring back, or to originate," since the One who is able to do this is God, glory be to Him. As for those who say, "God wills something, and I will the opposite, so my will is accomplished and God's will is not," arrogance is more fitting for this speaker. Thus it is established that the interpretation they mentioned is corrupt. Among people there are those who said that this threat is specific to the Jews and Christians, and among them are those who said:

صفحة ٩

إنَّهُ مُخْتَصٌّ بِمُشْرِكِي العَرَبِ، قالَ القاضِي: يَجِبُ حَمْلُ الآيَةِ عَلى الكُلِّ مِنَ المُشَبِّهَةِ والمُجْبِرَةِ، وكَذَلِكَ كُلُّ مَن وصَفَ اللَّهَ بِما لا يَلِيقُ بِهِ نَفْيًا وإثْباتًا، فَأضافَ إلَيْهِ ما يَجِبُ تَنْزِيهُهُ عَنْهُ أوْ نَزَّهَهُ عَمّا يَجِبُ أنْ يُضافَ إلَيْهِ، فالكُلُّ مِنهم داخِلُونَ تَحْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ؛ لِأنَّهم كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ، فَتَخْصِيصُ الآيَةِ بِالمُجْبِرَةِ والمُشَبِّهَةِ أوِ اليَهُودِ والنَّصارى لا يَجُوزُ، واعْلَمْ أنّا لَوْ أجْرَيْنا هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَلى عُمُومِها كَما ذَكَرَهُ القاضِي لَزِمَهُ تَكْفِيرُ الأُمَّةِ؛ لِأنَّكَ لا تَرى فِرْقَةً مِن فِرَقِ الأُمَّةِ إلّا وقَدْ حَصَلَ بَيْنَهُمُ اخْتِلافٌ شَدِيدٌ في صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ألا تَرى أنَّهُ حَصَلَ الِاخْتِلافُ بَيْنَ أبِي هاشِمٍ وأهْلِ السُّنَّةِ في مَسائِلَ كَثِيرَةٍ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، ويَلْزَمُ عَلى قانُونِ قَوْلِ القاضِي تَكْفِيرُ أحَدِهِما، فَثَبَتَ أنَّهُ يَجِبُ أنْ يُحْمَلَ الكَذِبُ المَذْكُورُ في الآيَةِ عَلى ما إذا قَصَدَ الإخْبارَ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ مَعَ أنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أنَّهُ كاذِبٌ فِيما يَقُولُ، ومِثالُ هَذا كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ فَإنَّهم كانُوا يَصِفُونَ تِلْكَ الأصْنامَ بِالإلَهِيَّةِ مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ بِالضَّرُورَةِ أنَّها جَماداتٌ، وكانُوا يَقُولُونَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى حَرَّمَ البَحِيرَةَ والسّائِبَةَ والوَصِيلَةَ والحامَ، مَعَ أنَّهم كانُوا يُنْكِرُونَ القَوْلَ بِأنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ كَذا وأباحَ كَذا، وكانَ قائِلُهُ عالِمًا بِأنَّهُ كَذِبٌ، وإذا كانَ كَذَلِكَ فَإلْحاقُ مِثْلَ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهَذا الجاهِلِ الكَذّابِ الضّالِّ المُضِلِّ يَكُونُ مُناسِبًا، أمّا مَن لَمْ يَقْصِدْ إلّا الحَقَّ والصِّدْقَ لَكِنَّهُ أخْطَأ، يَبْعُدُ إلْحاقُ هَذا الوَعِيدِ بِهِ.

that it is specific to the idolaters of the Arabs. The judge (al-Qadi) said: the verse must be applied to all of the Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) and the Mujbira (determinists), and likewise every person who describes God, by negation or affirmation, in a manner unbefitting Him, attributing to Him what must be declared far from Him, or declaring Him far from what must be attributed to Him. All of them are included under this verse, because they lied against God. Therefore restricting the verse to the Mujbira and Mushabbiha, or to the Jews and Christians, is not permissible. Know that if we applied this verse to its generality, as the judge stated, it would entail declaring the entire community (ummah) to be disbelievers, because you will not find any sect of the community without a severe disagreement concerning the attributes of God, exalted is He. Do you not see that disagreement arose between Abu Hashim and the People of the Sunnah on many issues concerning God's attributes? According to the principle of the judge's view, one of them would have to be declared a disbeliever. Thus it is established that the lying mentioned in the verse must be understood as the case where one intends to report about a thing while knowing that he is lying in what he says. An example of this is the disbelievers of Quraysh, for they described those idols as divine while knowingly recognizing by necessity that they were inanimate objects, and they used to say that God had forbidden the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and the ham, while they denied the claim that God had forbidden such-and-such or permitted such-and-such, and the one who said it knew it was a lie. If that is so, then attaching this kind of threat to this ignorant, lying, misguided, and misleading person is appropriate. As for one who intended nothing but truth and sincerity but erred, it is far-fetched to attach this threat to him.

البَحْثُ الثّانِي: الكَلامُ في كَيْفِيَّةِ السَّوادِ الحاصِلِ في وُجُوهِهِمْ، والأقْرَبُ أنَّهُ سَوادٌ مُخالِفٌ لِسائِرِ أنْواعِ السَّوادِ، وهو سَوادٌ يَدُلُّ عَلى الجَهْلِ بِاللَّهِ والكَذِبِ عَلى اللَّهِ، وأقُولُ: إنَّ الجَهْلَ ظُلْمَةٌ، والظُّلْمَةُ تُتَخَيَّلُ كَأنَّها سَوادٌ، فَسَوادُ قُلُوبِهِمْ أوْجَبَ سَوادَ وُجُوهِهِمْ، وتَحْتَ هَذا الكَلامِ أسْرارٌ عَمِيقَةٌ مِن مَباحِثِ أحْوالِ القِيامَةِ، فَلَمّا ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ هَذا الوَعِيدَ أرْدَفَهُ بِالوَعْدِ فَقالَ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ الآيَةَ، قالَ القاضِي: المُرادُ بِهِ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ؛ إذْ لا يُوصَفُ بِالِاتِّقاءِ المُطْلَقِ إلّا مَن كانَ هَذا حالَهُ، فَيُقالُ لَهُ: أمْرُكَ عَجِيبٌ جِدًّا فَإنَّكَ قُلْتَ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يُحْمَلَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ عَلى الَّذِينَ قالُوا: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾ فَعَلى هَذا القانُونِ لَمّا تَقَدَّمَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿ويَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى بَعْدَهُ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وجَبَ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ هُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ذَلِكَ الكَذِبَ، فَهَذا يَقْتَضِي أنَّ كُلَّ مَن لَمْ يَتَّصِفْ بِذَلِكَ الكَذِبِ أنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ تَحْتَ ذَلِكَ الوَعْدِ المَذْكُورِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿ويُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ وأنْ يَكُونَ قَوْلُكَ: ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ المُرادُ مِنهُ مَنِ اتَّقى كُلَّ الكَبائِرِ فاسِدًا، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ التَّعَصُّبَ يَحْمِلُ الرَّجُلَ العاقِلَ عَلى الكَلِماتِ المُتَناقِضَةِ، بَلِ الحَقُّ أنْ تَقُولَ: المُتَّقِي هو الآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ، والآتِي بِالِاتِّقاءِ في صُورَةٍ واحِدَةٍ آتٍ بِمُسَمّى الِاتِّقاءِ، وبِهَذا الحَرْفِ قُلْنا: الأمْرُ المُطْلَقُ لا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرارَ، ثُمَّ ذَلِكَ الِاتِّقاءُ غَيْرُ مَذْكُورٍ بِعَيْنِهِ في هَذِهِ اللَّفْظَةِ فَوَجَبَ حَمْلُهُ عَلى الِاتِّقاءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ الَّذِي سَبَقَ ذِكْرَهُ، وهَذا هو الكَذِبُ عَلى اللَّهِ تَعالى، فَثَبَتَ أنَّ ظاهِرَ الآيَةِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ مَنِ اتَّقى عَنْ تِلْكَ الصِّفَةِ وجَبَ دُخُولُهُ تَحْتَ هَذا الوَعْدِ الكَرِيمِ.

The second investigation concerns the manner of the blackness that appears on their faces. The closest view is that it is a blackness different from all other kinds of blackness, one that indicates ignorance of God and lying against God. I say: ignorance is darkness, and darkness is imagined as if it were blackness; so the blackness of their hearts necessitated the blackness of their faces. Beneath this discussion lie profound secrets from the investigations into the conditions of the Resurrection. When God mentioned this threat, He followed it with a promise, saying: "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and so on. The judge said: what is meant by it is the one who was mindful of all the major sins, since "mindfulness" in an absolute sense is not ascribed except to one whose state is this. It is said to him: your position is extremely strange, for you said, when the words of the Exalted were mentioned, "If only God had guided me, I would have been among the mindful," it is necessary that His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," be understood as referring to those who said, "If only God had guided me." By this principle, when His words, "On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces blackened," preceded, and then He, Exalted, said after it, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," it must be that the intended ones are those who were mindful of that lying. This implies that everyone who was not characterized by that lying is included under that promise mentioned in His words, "And God will deliver those who were mindful of Him to their place of salvation," and that your saying, "those who were mindful," meaning those who were mindful of all the major sins, is corrupt. Thus it is established that partisanship drives an intelligent man to contradictory statements. Rather, the truth is that you should say: the mindful one is the one who performs mindfulness, and the one who performs mindfulness in a single instance has performed the designation of mindfulness. And by this very letter we said: an absolute command does not indicate repetition. Then that mindfulness is not specified by name in this expression, so it must be understood as mindfulness regarding the thing previously mentioned, and this is lying against God, the Exalted. Thus it is established that the apparent meaning of the verse requires that whoever was mindful regarding that attribute must be included under this noble promise.

* * *

Then He, Exalted, said: "bi-mafazatihim" (with their place of salvation). Concerning this there are several issues:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قَرَأ حَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ ”بِمَفازاتِهِمْ“ عَلى الجَمْعِ، والباقُونَ بِمَفازَتِهِمْ عَلى التَّوْحِيدِ، وحَكى الواحِدِيُّ عَنِ الفَرّاءِ أنَّهُ قالَ: كِلاهُما صَوابٌ؛ إذْ يُقالُ في الكَلامِ: قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ أمْرُ القَوْمِ،

صفحة ١٠

وأُمُورُ القَوْمِ، قالَ أبُو عَلِيٍّ الفارِسِيُّ: الإفْرادُ لِلْمَصْدَرِ ووَجْهُ الجَمْعِ أنَّ المَصادِرَ قَدْ تُجْمَعُ إذا اخْتَلَفَتْ أجْناسُها، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَ﴾ [الأحْزابِ: ١٠] ولا شَكَّ أنَّ لِكُلِّ مُتَّقٍ نَوْعًا آخَرَ مِنَ المَفازَةِ.

First issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read "bi-mafazatihim" in the plural (*mafazatihim*), while the rest read *bi-mafazatihim* in the singular. Al-Wahidi related from al-Farra' that he said: both are correct, since it is said in speech: "the matter of the people has become clear," and "the affairs of the people." Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the singular is the verbal noun (masdar), and the reason for the plural is that verbal nouns may be pluralized when their kinds differ, as in the words of the Exalted: "and you assume about God assumptions" (al-Ahzab 33:10). There is no doubt that each one who is mindful has a different kind of salvation.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: المَفازَةُ مَفْعَلَةٌ مِنَ الفَوْزِ وهو السَّعادَةُ، فَكَأنَّ المَعْنى أنَّ النَّجاةَ في القِيامَةِ حَصَلَتْ بِسَبَبِ فَوْزِهِمْ في الدُّنْيا بِالطّاعاتِ والخَيْراتِ، فَعَبَّرَ عَنِ الفَوْزِ بِأوْقاتِها ومَواضِعِها.

Second issue: *al-mafazah* is of the form *mafalah* (a noun of place or time, *maf'alah*) derived from *al-fawz*, which is success or felicity. So the meaning seems to be that the deliverance on the Day of Resurrection was achieved through their success in this world by means of acts of obedience and good deeds; thus He expressed the success by its times and places.

ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ والمُرادُ أنَّهُ كالتَّفْسِيرِ لِتِلْكَ النَّجاةِ، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: كَيْفَ يُنَجِّيهِمْ؟ فَقِيلَ: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ وهَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ جامِعَةٌ؛ لِأنَّهُ إذا عَلِمَ أنَّهُ لا يَمَسُّهُ السُّوءُ كانَ فارِغَ البالِ بِحَسْبِ الحالِ عَمّا وقَعَ في قَلْبِهِ بِسَبَبِ فَواتِ الماضِي، فَحِينَئِذٍ يَظْهَرُ أنَّهُ سَلِمَ عَنْ كُلِّ الآفاتِ، ونَسْألُ اللَّهَ الفَوْزَ بِهَذِهِ الدَّرَجاتِ بِمَنِّهِ وكَرَمِهِ.

Then He said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." The meaning is that this is like an explanation of that deliverance, as if it were said: how will He deliver them? So it was said: "No evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve." This is a comprehensive expression, because when one knows that evil will not touch him, he is at ease in his state regarding what had occurred in his heart through the loss of the past. Then it becomes evident that he is safe from every calamity. We ask God for success in attaining these ranks by His bounty and generosity.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: دَلَّتِ الآيَةُ عَلى أنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ لا يَنالُهُمُ الخَوْفُ والرُّعْبُ في القِيامَةِ، وتَأكَّدَ هَذا بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ .

Third issue: the verse indicates that the believers will not be touched by fear or terror on the Day of Resurrection, and this is confirmed by His words: "The greatest terror will not grieve them" (al-Anbiya' 21:103).

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 39, verses 63–64:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is over all things a Guardian.﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah – those are the losers.﴾ ﴿Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"﴾ ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you should associate others with Allah, your work will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ ﴿Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.﴾

Know that when He had prolonged His discourse on explaining the promise and the threat, He returned to the proofs of divinity and monotheism. In this verse there are several issues:

**The first issue:** We have mentioned in Surah al-An'am that our companions (the Ash'aris) relied on His saying, ﴿Creator of all things﴾, to argue that the actions of servants are created by Allah, the Exalted, and we elaborated there on the questions and answers. There is no benefit in repeating them here, except that al-Ka'bi (al-Ka'bi) said certain words here, so we will mention them and answer them. He said: Allah, the Exalted, praised Himself by saying, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾, and it is not a form of praise that He should create disbelief and ugly deeds. Therefore the opponent cannot validly argue with it. Furthermore, in the early part of this community there was no disagreement about the actions of servants; rather, the disagreement between them and the Magians (al-Majus) and the Zindiqs (heretics) concerned the creation of diseases, predatory beasts and vermin. So Allah, the Exalted, wanted to make clear that all of these are of His creation. Also, the word "all" (kull) does not necessarily imply generality, as in His saying, ﴿And she has been given of everything﴾ (An-Naml 27:23), and ﴿destroying everything﴾ (Al-Ahqaf 46:25). Also, if the actions of servants were of Allah's creation, He would not have attributed them to them in His saying, ﴿disbelievers out of envy from themselves﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:109), and His saying, ﴿And they say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah﴾ (Al-Imran 3:78) would not be valid, nor would His saying, ﴿And We did not create the heaven and earth and what is between them in vain﴾ (Sad 38:27) be valid. This is the sum of what al-Ka'bi mentioned in his interpretation. Al-Jubba'i said: Allah is the Creator of all things except the actions of His creatures, for which commands and prohibitions are valid and for which they deserve reward and punishment. If their actions were a creation of Allah, the Exalted, this would not be permissible concerning Him, just as the like of it is not permissible concerning their colours and forms. Abu Muslim said: Creation (khalq) means determination (taqdir), not bringing into existence (ijad). So when Allah informs about His servants that they will do such-and-such an act, He has determined that act, and it is valid to say that He created it, even if He did not bring it into existence.

Know that the answer to these arguments has been given in full detail in Surah al-An'am, so whoever wishes to examine it should consult that topic in this book. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying, ﴿and He is over all things a Guardian﴾, the meaning is that all things are entrusted to Him; He is the one who maintains their preservation and management without any rival or partner. This also indicates that the act of the servant is created by Allah, the Exalted, because if the act of the servant occurred by the creation of the servant, that act would not be entrusted to Allah, the Exalted, and Allah would not be a Guardian over it, and that contradicts the generality of the verse.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.﴾ The meaning is that He, glorified be He, is the owner of their affairs and their Guardian. This is from the category of kinayah (figurative expression by implication), because the keeper of treasuries and the manager of their affairs is the one in whose hand are their keys. From this comes the saying of people, "So-and-so has been handed the keys of the kingdom." The word means keys (al-mafatih). The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It has no singular from its own form." It was also said: miqlid and maqalid, and it was said: miqlad and maqalid, like miftah and mafatih, and it was said: iqlid and aqalid. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "The word is originally Persian, but when the people Arabicized it, it became Arabic."

Know that the discussion of the interpretation of His saying, ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, is close to the discussion of His saying, ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ (Al-An'am 6:59), and the full treatment has already passed there. It is said: Uthman asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the interpretation of His saying, ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, and he (ﷺ) said: "O Uthman, no one has asked me about it before you. Its interpretation is: There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power and no strength except by Allah. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden; in His hand is the good; He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things Capable." Thus the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted it.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah – those are the losers.﴾ In this there are two issues:

**The first issue:** The apparent meaning of the verse requires that there is no loser except a disbeliever, and this indicates that everyone who is not a disbeliever will certainly receive a share of Allah's mercy.

**The second issue:** The author of al-Kashshaf raised a question: With what is His saying, ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾, connected? He answered that it is connected to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah will save those who feared Him﴾ (Az-Zumar 39:61), meaning Allah will save the God-fearing with their triumph; ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah – those are the losers.﴾ Between them, there intervened the statement that He is the Creator of all things, and that ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.﴾ I say: This is weak in my view for two reasons. First: the placement of a large intervening phrase between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined is far-fetched. Second: His saying, ﴿And Allah will save those who feared Him with their triumph﴾, is a verbal sentence (jumlah fi'liyyah), while His saying, ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah – those are the losers﴾, is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah), and conjoining a nominal sentence to a verbal sentence is not permissible. Rather, what is closer to me is that when Allah, the Exalted, described Himself with divine and majestic attributes – that He is the Creator of all things and that He is the owner of the keys of the heavens and the earth in their entirety – He said after that: ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ with these manifest and dazzling signs, ﴿those are the losers.﴾

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "Do you order me to worship other than Allah, O you ignorant ones?"﴾ And in this there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn ʿĀmir read (تَأْمُرُونَنِي, ta'murūnanī) with two nūns, the yāʾ having sukūn, and it is likewise in the Qur'an codices of Syria. Al-Wāḥidī said: this is the original form. Ibn Kathīr read (تَأْمُرُونِّي, ta'murūnnī) with a doubled nūn, the first nūn being given sukūn and assimilated into the second. Nāfiʿ read (تَأْمُرُونِي, ta'murūnī) with a single light nūn, by eliding one of the two nūns. The rest read it with a single kasrah-vowelled, doubled nūn.

The second issue: ﴿أفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ﴾ (afa-ghayra Allāh) is in the accusative, governed by (أعْبُدُ, aʿbudu), and ﴿تَأْمُرُونِّي﴾ (ta'murūnnī) is a parenthetical insertion. Its meaning is: "Shall I worship other than Allah at your command?" This was when the polytheists said to him: "Embrace the religion of some of our gods, and we will believe in your God." I say: a parallel to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ [al-Anʿām: 14], and we have already mentioned in that verse the wisdom behind placing the verb first.

The third issue: He described them as ignorant only because the description of the deity had preceded, as the Creator of things and the Possessor of the keys of the heavens and the earth, and it is evident that these idols are inanimate objects that neither harm nor benefit. Whoever turns away from worshipping the God described with those noble and holy attributes, and occupies himself with worshipping these base bodies, has reached a degree of ignorance beyond which there is none. For this reason He said: ﴿O you ignorant ones﴾. And there is no doubt that describing them with this is fitting in this context.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will surely be among the losers."﴾ Know that a complete discussion, with strong proofs and answers to doubts concerning the question of nullification (iḥbāṭ), has already been mentioned in Sūrat al-Baqarah, so we will not repeat it. The author of al-Kashshāf (al-Kashshāf, the Qur'an commentary of al-Zamakhsharī) said: it was read as (لَيُحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ, layuḥbaṭanna ʿamaluka) in the passive voice, and it was read with the yāʾ and nūn, i.e., "layuḥbiṭanna Allāh" (Allah will nullify), or "al-shirk" (polytheism). There are questions on the verse:

The first question: How was it revealed to him and to those before him while they were, specifically, in a state of polytheism? The answer: the sense of the verse is: "It has been revealed to you: if you associate partners, your deeds will be nullified; and to those before you the same." Or: "It has been revealed to you and to each one of them: if you associate partners," just as you say: "He clothed us with a robe," meaning each one of us.

The second question: What is the difference between the two lāms? The answer: the first is the lām preparing for the omitted oath, and the second is the lām of the response.

The third question: How is this statement valid, given Allah's knowledge that His messengers do not associate partners and their deeds are not nullified? The answer: His saying: ﴿If you associate partners, your deeds will be nullified﴾ is a conditional proposition, and the truth of a conditional proposition does not necessitate the truth of its two parts. Do you not see that your saying: "If the number five were even, it would be divisible into two equal parts" is a true proposition, although each of its two parts is not true? Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿If there were in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 22], and it does not follow from this that it is true that there are gods in them, or that they have both been ruined.

The fourth question: What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and you will surely be among the losers﴾? The answer: just as the acts of obedience of the prophets and messengers are superior to the acts of obedience of others, so too the wrongs that proceed from them would be worse; for they, by the supposition of their occurrence, would be graver. This is consistent with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We would have made you taste double in life and double in death﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 75]. So the meaning is "double the polytheism that would result from him", and by supposing it occurred from him, its effect on the side of Allah's wrath would be stronger and greater.

It is as if He said: "You order me to worship none but other than Allah," because His saying ﴿Say, "Do you order me to worship other than Allah?"﴾ indicates that they had specified for him the worship of other than Allah.
