Then He said: ﴿and be among the thankful﴾, for what He guided you to: that it is not permissible to worship except the God who is All-Powerful absolutely, All-Knowing, All-Wise, and for what He directed you to: that it is obligatory to turn away from worshipping everything other than Allah.

قَوْلُهُ تعالى: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ ﴿ونُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ إلّا مَن شاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرى فَإذا هم قِيامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ ﴿وأشْرَقَتِ الأرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّها ووُضِعَ الكِتابُ وجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ والشُّهَداءِ وقُضِيَ بَيْنَهم بِالحَقِّ وهم لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ ﴿ووُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما عَمِلَتْ وهو أعْلَمُ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ﴾

واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى عن المشركين أنهم أمروا الرسولَ بعبادة الأصنام، ثم إنه تعالى أقام الدلائل على فساد قولهم وأمر الرسولَ بأن يعبد الله ولا يعبد شيئًا آخر سواه، بيّن أنهم لو عرفوا الله حق معرفته لما جعلوا هذه الأشياء الخسيسة مشاركةً له في المعبودية، فقال: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾. وفي الآية مسائل:

المسألة الأولى: احتجّ بعض الناس بهذه الآية على أن الخلق لا يعرفون حقيقة الله، قالوا: لأن قوله: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ يفيد هذا المعنى. إلا أنا ذكرنا أن هذا صفةُ حالِ الكفار، فلا يلزم من وصف الكفار بأنهم ما قدروا الله حق قدره وصفُ المؤمنين بذلك، فسقط هذا الكلام.

المسألة الثانية: قوله: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ أي ما عظّموه حق تعظيمه، وهذه الآية مذكورة في سور ثلاث: في سورة الأنعام، وفي سورة الحج، وفي هذه السورة.

واعلم أنه تعالى لما بيّن أنهم ما عظّموه تعظيمًا لائقًا به أردفه بما يدل على كمال عظمته ونهاية جلالته، فقال: ﴿والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾. قال القفّال (al-Qaffal): ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ كقولِ القائلِ: وما قَدَرْتَنِي حَقَّ قَدْرِي وأنا الذي فعلتُ كذا وكذا، أي لما عرفتَ أن حالي وصفتي هذا الذي ذكرتُ، فوجب أن لا تحُطَّني عن قدري ومنزلتي. ونظيرُه قوله تعالى:
[Page 14]
﴿كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وكُنْتُمْ أمْواتًا فَأحْياكُمْ﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨]، أي كيف تكفرون بمن هذا وصفُه وحالُ مُلكه؟ فكذا هاهنا، والمعنى ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ إذ زعموا أن له شركاء وأنه لا يقدر على إحياء الموتى، مع أن الأرض والسماوات في قبضته وقدرته. قال صاحب "الكشاف" (al-Kashshaf): الغرض من هذا الكلام إذا أخذتَه كما هو بجملته ومجموعه تصويرُ عظمته والتوقيفُ على كنه جلاله، من غير ذهاب بالقبضة ولا باليمين إلى جهة حقيقةٍ أو مجاز. وكذلك ما «رُوِيَ أنّ يهوديًّا جاء إلى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا أبا القاسم، إنّ الله يُمسك السماوات يوم القيامة على إصبع، والأرضين على إصبع، والجبال على إصبع، والشجر على إصبع، والثرى على إصبع، وسائر الخلق على إصبع، ثم يَهُزّهنّ فيقول: أنا الملك! فضحك رسولُ الله ﷺ تعجبًا مما قال».

قال صاحب "الكشاف": وإنما ضحك أفصحُ العرب لأنه لم يفهم منه إلا ما يفهمه علماءُ البيان، من غير تصوّر إمساكٍ ولا إصبعٍ ولا هَزٍّ ولا شيءٍ من ذلك، ولكنّ فهمَه وقع أولَ كلِّ شيءٍ وآخرَه على الزبدةِ والخلاصةِ التي هي الدلالةُ على القدرة الباهرة، وأن الأفعال العظام التي تتحير فيها الأوهام ولا تكتنهها الأذهان هيّنةٌ عليه. قال: ولا نرى بابًا في علم البيان أدقَّ ولا ألطفَ من هذا الباب. فيُقال له: هل تُسلِّم أن الأصل في الكلام حملُه على الحقيقة (haqiqa، المعنى الحرفي الأصلي)، وأنه إنما يُعدَل عن الحقيقة إلى المجاز (majaz، المعنى المجازي) عند قيام الدلالة على أن حملَه على حقيقته ممتنعٌ، فحينئذٍ يجب حملُه على المجاز؟ فإن أنكر هذا الأصل، فحينئذٍ يخرج القرآنُ بالكلية عن أن يكون حجةً، فإنّ لكل أحدٍ أن يقول: المقصودُ من الآية الفلانية كذا وكذا، فأنا أحمل الآية على ذلك المقصود، ولا ألتفت إلى الظواهر. مثاله: من تمسك بالآيات الواردة في ثواب أهل الجنة وعقاب أهل النار، قال: المقصود بيانُ سعادات المطيعين وشقاوة المذنبين، وأنا أحمل هذه الآيات على هذا المقصود ولا أُثبت الأكلَ والشربَ ولا سائرَ الأحوال الجسمانية. ومن تمسك بالآيات الواردة في إثبات وجوب الصلاة فقال: المقصود منه إيجابُ تنوير القلب بذكر الله، فأنا أكتفي بهذا القدر ولا أُوجب هذه الأعمال المخصوصة. وإذا عرفتَ الكلام في هذين المثالين فقِسْ عليه سائرَ المسائل الأصولية والفروعية، وحينئذٍ يخرج القرآنُ عن أن يكون حجةً في المسائل الأصولية والفروعية، وذلك باطلٌ قطعًا.

وأما إن سلّم أن الأصل في علم القرآن أن يُعتقد أن الأصل في الكلام حملُه على حقيقته، فإن قام دليلٌ منفصلٌ على أنه يتعذر حملُه على حقيقته، فحينئذٍ يتعين صرفُه إلى مجازه، فإن حصلت هناك مجازاتٌ لم يتعيّن صرفُه إلى مجازٍ معيّن إلا إذا كان الدليل يوجب ذلك التعيين، فنقول هاهنا: لفظُ القبضة ولفظُ اليمين حقيقةٌ في الجارحة المخصوصة، ولا يمكنك أن تصرف ظاهرَ الكلام عن هذا المعنى إلا إذا أقمتَ الدلالةَ على أن حملَ هذه الألفاظ على ظواهرها ممتنعٌ، فحينئذٍ يجب حملُها على المجازات، ثم تبيّن بالدليل أن المعنى الفلانيَّ يصح جعلُه مجازًا عن تلك الحقيقة، ثم تبيّن بالدليل أن هذا المجاز أولى من غيره. وإذا ثبتت هذه المقدمات وترتيبُها على هذا الوجه، فهذا هو الطريق الصحيح الذي عليه تعويلُ أهل التحقيق، فأنت ما أتيتَ في هذا الباب بطريقةٍ جديدة وكلامٍ غريب، بل هو عينُ ما ذكره أهل التحقيق، فثبت أن الفرحَ الذي أظهره من أنه اهتدى إلى الطريق الذي لم يعرفه غيرُه، طريقٌ فاسد، دالٌّ على قلّة وقوفه على المعاني.

ولنرجعْ إلى الطريق الحقيقي، فنقول: لا شكَّ أن لفظَ القبضة واليمين مُشعِرٌ بهذه الأعضاء والجوارح، إلا أن الدلائل العقلية قامت على امتناع ثبوت الأعضاء والجوارح لله تعالى، فوجب حملُ هذه الأعضاء على وجوه المجاز، فنقول: إنه يُقال: فلانٌ في قبضة فلانٍ إذا كان تحت تدبيره وتسخيره. قال تعالى: ﴿إلّا عَلى أزْواجِهِمْ أوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُمْ﴾ [المعارج: ٣٠]، والمرادُ منه كونُه مملوكًا له، ويُقال: هذه الدارُ
[Page 15]
في يد فلان، وفلانٌ صاحبُ اليد، والمرادُ من الكل القدرةُ. والفقهاءُ يقولون في الشروط: وقبض فلانٌ كذا وصار في قبضته، ولا يريدون إلا خلوصَ مُلكه. وإذا ثبت تعذّرُ حمل هذه الألفاظ على حقائقها وجب حملُها على مجازاتها؛ صونًا لهذه النصوص عن التعطيل. فهذا هو الكلامُ الحقيقيُّ في هذا الباب، ولنا كتابٌ مفردٌ في إثبات تنزيه الله تعالى عن الجسمية والمكان، سمّيناه "تأسيس التقديس"، من أراد الإطنابَ في هذا الباب فليرجعْ إليه.

* * *

المسألة الثالثة: في تفسير ألفاظ الآية. قوله: ﴿والأرْضُ﴾ المرادُ منه الأرضون السبعُ، ويدل عليه وجوهٌ:

الأول: قوله: ﴿جَمِيعًا﴾، فإن هذا التأكيدَ لا يحسن إدخالُه إلا على الجمع، ونظيرُه قوله: ﴿كُلُّ الطَّعامِ﴾ [آل عمران: ٩٣]، وقوله تعالى: ﴿أوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلى عَوْراتِ النِّساءِ﴾ [النور: ٣١]، وقوله تعالى: ﴿والنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ﴾ [ق: ١٠]، وقوله تعالى: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ إلّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ [العصر: ٢، ٣]، فإن هذه الألفاظ الملِحّةَ باللفظ المفرد تدل على أن المرادَ منه الجمعُ، فكذا هاهنا.

والثاني: أنه قال بعدَه: ﴿والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٌ﴾ فوجب أن يكون المرادُ بالأرض الأرضون.

الثالث: أن الموضعَ موضعُ تعظيمٍ وتفخيمٍ، فهذا مقتضى المبالغة. وأما القبضةُ فهي المرّةُ الواحدةُ من القبض، قال تعالى: ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِن أثَرِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ [طه: ٩٦]، والقَبضةُ بالضم المقدارُ المقبوضُ بالكف، ويُقال أيضًا: أعطني قَبضةً من كذا، يريد معنى القبضةِ تسميةً بالمصدر، والمعنى: والأرضون جميعًا قبضتُه، أي ذواتُ قبضته يقبضهنّ قبضةً واحدةً من قبَضاته، يعني أن الأرضين مع ما لها من العظمة والبَسطة لا يبلغن إلا قبضةً واحدةً من قبَضاته. أما إذا أُريد معنى القبضة فظاهرٌ؛ لأن المعنى أن الأرضين بجملتها مقدارُ ما يقبضه بكفٍّ واحدة. فإن قيل: ما وجهُ قراءة من قرأ (قَبْضَتَهُ) بالنصب؟ قلنا: جعل القبضةَ ظرفًا. وقوله: ﴿مَطْوِيّاتٌ﴾ من الطيِّ الذي هو ضدُّ النشر، كما قال تعالى: ﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٤]، وعادةُ طاوي السجلِّ أن يطويَه بيمينه. ثم قال صاحب "الكشاف": وقيل: قبضتُه مُلكُه، ويمينُه قدرتُه، وقيل: مطويّاتٌ بيمينه؛ أي مفنيّاتٌ بقسمه؛ لأنه أقسم أن يقبضها.

ولما ذكر هذه الوجوه عاد إلى القول الأول بأنها وجوهٌ ركيكة، وأن حملَ هذا الكلام على محضِ التمثيل أولى، وبالغ في تقرير هذا الكلام فأطنب. وأقول: إن حالَ هذا الرجل في إقدامه على تحسين طريقته وتقبيح طريقةِ القدماء عجيبٌ جدًّا، فإنه إن كان مذهبُه أنه يجوز ترك ظاهر اللفظ والمصيرُ إلى المجاز من غير دليل، فهذا طعنٌ في القرآن وإخراجٌ له عن أن يكون حجةً في شيءٍ، وإن كان مذهبُه أن الأصل في الكلام الحقيقةُ، وأنه لا يجوز العدولُ عنه إلا لدليل منفكٍّ، فهذه هي الطريقةُ التي أطبق عليها جمهورُ المتقدمين، فأين الكلامُ الذي يزعم أنه علِمه؟ وأين العلمُ الذي لم يعرفه غيرُه؟ مع أنه وقع في التأويلات العُسرِ والكلماتِ الركيكة. فإن قالوا: المرادُ أنه لما دلّ الدليلُ على أنه ليس المرادُ من لفظ القبضة واليمين هذه الأعضاءَ، وجب علينا أن نكتفيَ بهذا القدر ولا نشتغلَ بتعيين المراد، بل نفوّض علمَه إلى الله تعالى، فنقول: هذا هو طريقُ الموحِّدين الذين يقولون: إنا نعلم أنه ليس مرادُ الله من هذه الألفاظ هذه الأعضاءَ، فأما تعيينُ المراد، فإنا نفوّض ذلك العلمَ إلى الله تعالى، فهذه هي طريقةُ السلف المعرِضين عن التأويلات، فثبت أن هذه التأويلاتِ التي أتى بها هذا الرجلُ ليس تحتها شيءٌ من الفائدة أصلًا، والله أعلم.
[Page 16]
واعلم أنه تعالى لما بيّن عظمتَه من الوجه الذي تقدم قال: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾، يعني أن هذا القادرَ القاهرَ العظيمَ الذي حارت العقولُ والألبابُ في وصف عظمته، تنزّه وتقدّس عن أن تُجعل الأصنامُ شركاءَ له في المعبودية. فإن قيل: السؤالُ على هذا الكلام من وجوه:

الأول: أن العرشَ أعظمُ من السماوات السبع والأرضين السبع، ثم إنه قال في صفة العرش: ﴿ويَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهم يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمانِيَةٌ﴾ [الحاقة: ١٧]، وإذا وصف الملائكةَ بكونهم حاملين العرشَ العظيمَ، فكيف يجوز تقديرُ عظمةِ الله بكونه حاملًا للسماوات والأرض؟

Second question: the verse says, ﴿And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens folded in His right hand﴾, which describes a state that will occur only on the Day of Resurrection, and the people addressed had not witnessed it. If this address is to those who affirm the prophets, then they would already acknowledge that it is impermissible to say that idols are partners of Allah, so there is no benefit in presenting this argument against them. And if this address is to those who deny prophethood, and they deny His saying, ﴿And the earth entirely in His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾, then how can it be used as evidence to refute the claim of associating partners with Him?
* * *
Third question: the essential meaning of the "grip" and the "right hand" is complete and perfect power to preserve these great bodies. Just as their preservation and holding on the Day of Resurrection is by none other than the power of Allah, so too is it now. Then what is the benefit in restricting these states to the Day of Resurrection?

The answer to the first: the degrees of exalting are many, and the first of them is establishing the greatness of Allah by His being capable of preserving these great bodies. Then, after establishing His greatness by His being capable of holding those angels who carry the Throne.

The answer to the second: the intended meaning is that the Truth, glorified is He, is the one who takes charge of keeping the heavens and the earths in their state of being inhabited at this time, and He is the one who takes charge of ruining and annihilating them on the Day of Resurrection. This indicates the attainment of complete power over bringing into existence and bringing to non-existence, and also an alert that He is absolutely self-sufficient, for it indicates that when He wishes to ruin the earth, it is as if He grasps a small handful and intends to annihilate it, and this indicates perfect independence.

The answer to the third: He only restricted those states to the Day of Resurrection so as to show that just as the perfection of His power in bringing into existence appeared at the building of the world, so too the perfection of His power appeared at the ruin of the world. And Allah knows best.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had described the perfection of His greatness by what has preceded its mention, He followed it with the mention of another method that also indicates the perfection of His power and greatness, and that is the explanation of the preliminaries of the Day of Resurrection, because the blowing of the Trumpet occurs before that day. So He said: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on﴾. And they differed concerning the "ṣa'qah" (the falling in a swoon).

Some of them said: it is other than death, based on His saying, exalted is He, concerning Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious﴾ [al-A'raf: 143], although he did not die. So this is the blast that causes intense terror, and according to this interpretation the meaning of the blast of the swoon and the blast of terror is one and the same, and it is what is mentioned in Surat an-Naml in His saying: ﴿And the day the Trumpet is blown, those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified﴾. And according to this view, the blowing of the Trumpet is only twice.

The second view: the ṣa'qah is an expression for death. Those who hold this view said: they die from terror and intensity of the sound. According to this interpretation, the blast occurs three times: the first is the blast of terror, which is what is mentioned in Surat an-Naml; the second is the blast of the swoon; and the third is the blast of rising. The latter two are mentioned in this surah.
* * *
As for His saying: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, there are several opinions:

The first: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: at the blast of the swoon, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth dies except Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and the Angel of Death. Then Allah causes Mika'il and Israfil to die, and Jibril and the Angel of Death remain, and then He causes Jibril to die.

The second view: they are the martyrs, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169]. And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "They are the martyrs, hanging their swords around the Throne."

The third view: Jabir said: this excepted one is Musa, peace be upon him, because he was struck with a swoon once, so he is not struck with it a second time.

The fourth view: they are the wide-eyed houris and the inhabitants of the Throne and the Footstool.

The fifth view: Qatadah said: Allah knows best who they are, and there is nothing in the Qur'an and the reports that indicates who they are.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾. On this there are several discussions:

The first: The wording of the Qur'an indicates that this blast is later than the first blast, because the word "thumma" (then, indicating a lapse of time) denotes delay. Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The Qur'an indicates that this is the first blast. It has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "between the two there are forty..." but I do not know whether it means forty days, or forty months, or forty years, or forty thousand years.

The second: His saying "ukhra" (another) — the implied sense is: "And the Trumpet will be blown, one blast, then another blast will be blown in it." The omission is acceptable because "ukhra" points to it and because it is known.

The third: His saying "fa-idha hum qiyam" (and behold, they are standing) means their standing up from the graves occurs immediately after this final blast, without delay, because the "fa" (then, immediately) in His saying "fa-idha hum" indicates immediate sequence.

The fourth: His saying "yanzurun" (looking on). On this there are two interpretations. The first: they will be "yanzurun," meaning they will turn their eyes in all directions, like the gaze of one stunned when a great calamity suddenly overtakes him. The second: they will be "yanzurun" to see what will be done to them. It is also possible that "qiyam" means standing still and motionless in a place, because bewilderment and awe have overcome them.

When Allah, exalted is He, had explained these two blasts, He said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾. On this there are several issues:

The first issue: This earth mentioned is not the earth on which people sit now, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿On the day when the earth will be replaced by another earth﴾ [Ibrahim: 48], and by His saying: ﴿And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with one blow﴾ [al-Haqqah: 14]. Rather, it is another earth which Allah creates for the assembly of the Day of Resurrection.

The second issue: The Mujassima (anthropomorphists) said: Allah, exalted is He, is pure light. So when Allah is present on that earth to judge between His servants, that earth shines with the light of Allah. They reinforced this with His saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

Know that the answer to this objection is from several aspects:

The first: We have explained in the commentary on His saying ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ that it is not permissible that Allah, glorified and exalted, be light in the sense of being of the same kind as these visible lights. We explained that when a literal reading of the speech is impossible, the word "light" here must be taken to mean "justice." So here we need to show that the word "light" is used with this meaning, and then to show that the intended meaning of the word "light" here is nothing but this meaning. As for showing its usage, people say to a just king: "The horizons have shone with your justice, and the world has been illuminated by your equity," just as they say: "The lands have been darkened by your oppression." As for showing that the intended meaning of light here is only justice, He said: ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾, and it is known that the bringing of the witnesses is only to manifest justice. It does not follow that this is an attribute of Allah's essence, because mere minimal cause suffices for the truth of an attribution. Since that light is among the creations of Allah and He honored it by attributing it to Himself, that light is "the light of Allah," like His saying: "the House of Allah" and "the she-camel of Allah." This answer is stronger than the first, because in this answer there is no need to abandon the literal sense and go to a figurative one.

The third aspect: It is said: "So-and-so is the lord of this land, the lord of this house, the lord of this slave-girl." It is not far-fetched that the lord of this land is a king among kings, and on this assumption there is no impediment to his being "light."

The third issue: He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse several things about that day:

The first of them: His saying ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾, on which the discussion has already passed.

The second: His saying ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. Regarding what is meant by "the Book" there are several views. The first: it is the Preserved Tablet, in which is recorded the account of the states of the world of this life until the Hour of Resurrection. The second: what is meant is the books of deeds, as Allah, exalted is He, said in Surah al-Isra: ﴿And every person's omen We have fastened to his neck, and We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find laid open﴾ [al-Isra: 13], and He also said in another verse: ﴿What is with this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but has enumerated it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you against these as a witness?﴾ [al-Nisa: 41], and He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say, "What response were you given?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109].

Muqatil said: it means the guardian angels (al-hafazah). This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21]. It was also said: He meant by "the witnesses" those martyred in the way of Allah.

The third: His saying ﴿and every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, meaning every soul will be paid the recompense for what it did. Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verses 71–72:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers."﴾ ﴿It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had described the condition of the people of the Resurrection in summary, saying, ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, He then explained the manner of the condition of the people of punishment, then the manner of the condition of the people of reward, and concluded the surah.

As for the description of the condition of the people of punishment, it is what is mentioned in this verse, namely His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups.﴾ Ibn Zaydan said: The driving of those who disbelieved to Hell occurs with force and pushing. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push﴾ [al-Tur: 13], meaning they will be pushed with a push. Its counterpart is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the one who repulses the orphan﴾ [al-Ma'un: 2], meaning he pushes him away. And it is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will drive the criminals to Hell like thirsty cattle﴾ [Maryam: 86].

As for zumar (groups), they are separate companies, one following another. Allah, exalted is He, made clear that they are driven to Hell, and when they reach it, its gates are opened. This indicates that the gates of Hell are only opened upon the arrival of those people at it. When they enter Hell, the keepers of Hell will say to them: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you﴾, meaning from your own kind, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day﴾. If it is asked: Why was the day attributed to them? We say: He meant the meeting of this your time, which is the time of their entering the Fire, not the Day of Resurrection. The use of the word "day" and "days" for times of hardship is widespread. Thereupon the disbelievers say: "Yes, they have indeed come to us and recited to us," ﴿but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers.﴾ In this verse there are two issues:

The first issue: the sense of the statement is that the word of punishment has come true against us, and one against whom the word of punishment has come true, how can he escape punishment? This is explicit that the happy one does not turn into a wretch, and the wretch does not turn into a happy one. The statements of the Mu'tazilah in repelling this statement are well known, and our answers to them are also well known.

The second issue: the verse indicates that there is no obligation before the coming of the Law, because the angels made clear that they had no cause or excuse left after the coming of the prophets, peace be upon them. Had the coming of the prophets not been a condition for deserving punishment, there would be no benefit in this statement. Then, when the angels heard this statement from them, they said to them: ﴿Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ The Mu'tazilah said: If their entering the Fire were because the word of punishment had come true against them, then the angels' saying ﴿Wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾ would have no benefit. Rather, this statement remains meaningful only if we say that they entered the Fire because they were arrogant toward the prophets, did not accept their word, and did not heed their proofs. This indicates the soundness of our view. And Allah knows best what is correct.

Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ The Mu'tazilah said: If their entering the Fire were because the word of punishment had come true against them, then the angels' saying ﴿Wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾ would have no benefit. Rather, this statement remains meaningful only if we say that they entered the Fire because they were arrogant toward the prophets, did not accept their word, and did not heed their proofs. This indicates the soundness of our view. And Allah knows best what is correct.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 39, verses 73–74:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups, until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it to abide therein." And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and given us the earth to inherit, that we may settle in the Garden wherever we will. How excellent is the reward of the workers!"﴾ ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting [Allah] with the praise of their Lord. And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained the conditions of the people of punishment in the previous verse, He explained in this verse the conditions of the people of reward. He said: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups.﴾ If it is said: driving [to the Fire] for punishment is understandable, since when they are commanded to go to the place of torment and misery, they must be driven to it; but as for the people of reward, when they are commanded to go to the place of honour, comfort and happiness, what need is there for driving?

The answer has several aspects:

The first: love and friendship remain among the God-fearing on the Day of Resurrection, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 67]. So when one of them is told, "Go to the Garden," he says, "I will not enter it until my beloved ones and my friends enter it," and so they hold back for this reason. Then they need to be driven to the Garden.

The second: those who feared their Lord worshipped Allah, exalted is He, neither for the Garden nor for the Fire. Thus the intensity of their absorption in witnessing the stations of majesty and beauty prevents them from desiring the Garden, so inevitably they need to be driven to the Garden.

The third: the Prophet ﷺ said: "The majority of the people of Paradise are the simple-minded, and the 'Illiyyun are for the righteous." Therefore for this reason they are driven to the Garden.

The fourth: both the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire are driven, but the meaning of driving the people of the Fire is thrusting them into it with humiliation and violence, as is done to a captive when he is led to prison and chains. The meaning of driving the people of the Garden is driving their mounts, because they are only taken there while riding; and the meaning of that driving is hastening them to the abode of honour and good pleasure, as is done with one who is honoured and esteemed among those who come to kings. How different is the one driving from the other.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them﴾, and so on. Know that this whole statement is a single conditional composed of several restrictions. The first restriction is their arrival at the Garden. The second restriction is His saying: ﴿and its gates are opened.﴾ If it is said: about the people of the Fire He said "its gates were opened" without the waw, while here He used the waw; what is the difference? We say: the difference is that the gates of Hell are not opened except when its people have entered it, whereas the opening of the gates of the Garden precedes their arrival there, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them﴾ [Sad: 50]. Therefore the waw was used, as if it were said: "until, when they reach it and its gates have already been opened."

The third restriction is His saying: ﴿and its keepers say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ He explained, exalted is He, that the keepers of the Garden address the people of reward with these three words. The first of them is their saying ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, which indicates that they give them the good news of safety from every calamity. The second is their saying ﴿you have done well﴾, meaning: you are purified from the filth of sins and cleansed from the impurity of faults. The third is their saying ﴿so enter it to abide therein﴾. The "fa" in His saying ﴿so enter it﴾ indicates that this entry is caused by goodness and purity. The Mu'tazilah said: this indicates that no one enters it except one who is free of all sins. We say: this is weak, because He, exalted is He, changes their evil deeds into good deeds, and then they become good and pure by the grace of Allah, exalted is He.

If it is said: this that has been mentioned is the condition, so where is the answer? We say: there are two views. The first: the answer is omitted, and the purpose of omitting it is to indicate that it has reached such perfection that it cannot be mentioned.

The second: the answer is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and its keepers said to them, "Peace be upon you"﴾, with the waw omitted. The correct view is the first. Then Allah, exalted is He, informed us that when the angels address the God-fearing with these words, the God-fearing say at that point: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us﴾ in His saying: ﴿Fear not, nor grieve, and rejoice in the Garden which you were promised﴾ [Fussilat: 30]; ﴿and given us the earth to inherit﴾ [az-Zumar: 74]. The "earth" here means the earth of the Garden. He expressed it by inheritance for several reasons:

The first: the Garden was at the beginning given to Adam, peace be upon him, since He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And eat from it in abundance wherever you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35]. When the Garden returned to the children of Adam, this was the cause of calling it an inheritance.

The second: this term is derived from the saying of one who says: "This deed bequeathed such-and-such, and this deed bequeathed such-and-such." Since their obedience had brought them the Garden, they therefore said: ﴿and given us the earth to inherit﴾. The meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, bequeathed us the Garden by enabling us to perform deeds that bequeathed the Garden.

The third: the heir disposes of what he inherits as he wills, without any contender or opponent. Likewise the believing God-fearing dispose of the Garden as they wish and desire. Resemblance is the basis for the goodness of a metaphor. If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿wherever we will﴾, and can one of them settle in another's place? We say: every person has a garden for which he does not need the garden of another. The wise men of Islam said: gardens are of two kinds: physical gardens and spiritual gardens. Physical gardens do not admit sharing in them, but spiritual things, their attainment by one does not prevent their attainment by others.

When Allah, exalted is He, described the attributes of the people of the Garden, He said: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers!﴾ Muqatil said: this is not the speech of the people of the Garden, but the speech of Allah, exalted is He; because when He related what took place between the angels and the God-fearing regarding the attribute of the reward of the people of the Garden, He said afterwards: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers!﴾ And when He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾, He mentioned after it the reward of the angels. Just as the abode of the reward of the God-fearing believers is the Garden, so the abode of the reward of the angels is the sides and edges of the Throne. Therefore He said: ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾, that is, encircling the Throne. Al-Layth said: it is said "ḥaffa al-qawm bi-sayyidihim" (the people encircled their chief) when they went around him.

Having understood this, we say: He, exalted is He, made clear that the abode of their reward is the sides and edges of the Throne. Then He said: ﴿exalting [Allah] with the praise of their Lord﴾, and this indicates that their reward is that very praise and glorification. Thus the sum of the statement returns to the conclusion that the greatest degree of reward is the absorption of the hearts of the servants in the degrees of transcendence and the stations of sanctification.

Then He said: ﴿And judgment will be passed between them with truth﴾. The meaning is that they are at different ranks and varying levels, so each of them has a fixed limit in the degrees of knowledge and obedience that he does not exceed or go beyond. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿And judgment will be passed between them with truth. And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ That is, when judgment has been passed between them with truth, the angels will say: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, for His judgment between us with truth. Here there is a subtle point higher than what came before. When He, glorified is He, passes judgment between them with truth, they do not praise Him on account of that judgment, but they praise Him by His necessary attribute, which is that He is Lord of the worlds. For whoever praises the Benefactor because his benefaction has reached him has, in reality, not praised the Benefactor but has praised the benefaction. As for whoever praises the Benefactor, not because a blessing has reached him, he has reached the depths of the sea of monotheism (tawhid). This holds if we say that His words ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ describe the state of the angels in reward. But if we say that it is part of the description of the reward of the believers, then the explanation is that when the God-fearing said ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and caused us to inherit the earth, that we may settle in Paradise wherever we will﴾, it became evident from them that in Paradise they occupy themselves with praising Allah and remembering Him with glorification and commendation. Then He, exalted is He, explained that just as the occupation of the God-fearing in Paradise is this praise and exaltation, so too the occupation of the angels who surround the Throne is praise and glorification. Moreover, the sides of the Throne are adjacent to the sides of Paradise. At that point it becomes clear that the believing God-fearing and the nearest angels come to agree on being absorbed in praising Allah and glorifying Him, and this was a cause of greater delight for them in that glorification and praise.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And judgment will be passed between them﴾, that is, between the human beings. Then He said: ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾. The meaning is that they put forward glorification (tasbih), and what is meant by it is declaring Allah free of everything unfitting to divinity.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾, what is meant is ascribing to Him the attributes of divinity. Thus tasbih is an expression for acknowledging His transcendence above everything unfitting to Him, which is the attributes of majesty (jalal). And His saying ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ is an expression for affirming that He is described by the attributes of divinity, which are the attributes of bounty and honour (ikram). The combination of the two is what is mentioned in His saying: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾ [al-Rahman: 78]. And this is what the angels used to mention before the creation of the world, which is their saying: ﴿And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾. In His saying ﴿And it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ there is another subtle point: He did not specify who that speaker is. The purpose of this vagueness is to alert that the final words of the intelligent in praising the presence of majesty and greatness are nothing other than saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. This is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He, concerning the people of Paradise: ﴿And the last of their prayer is, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10].

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The explanation (tafsir) of this surah was completed on the night of Tuesday, at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah, in the year six hundred and three.

The author of this book says: The nearest angels have been unable to count Your praise, so who am I? The messengers among the prophets have acknowledged their incapacity and shortcoming, so who am I? I have nothing except to say: You are You and I am I. From You comes mercy, grace, generosity and kindness, and from me comes incapacity, humiliation, failure and loss. O Most Merciful, O Judge, O Most Compassionate, O Bestower, pour upon me abundant mercy and forgiveness, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. May Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad (ﷺ), the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, his companions and his wives, the Mothers of the Believers, and grant them abundant peace.
